0g: 0G is a modular, Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for decentralized AI. It combines a smart-contract chain, cheap fast data storage, a data-availability layer and AI compute; the 0G token pays for services and staking.
1inch: 1inch (1INCH) is a DeFi aggregator of decentralized exchanges, founded in 2019 by Sergej Kunz and Anton Bukov. It looks for the best exchange rate by splitting a trade across many exchanges on different networks; the 1INCH token is used to govern the protocol.
2z: DoubleZero (2Z) is a protocol for a global fiber-optic network that moves data quickly between blockchain validators, above all on Solana, and trading systems. Independent fiber owners contribute links, and 2Z is the token that connects network users with these infrastructure providers.
a-token: Vaulta (A) is the layer-1 network that the EOS blockchain was renamed to in 2025, refocused on Web3 banking. It combines fast transactions with infrastructure for payments, Bitcoin yield via exSat and tokenized assets; EOS tokens were swapped for A.
aapl: Apple is a US technology company based in Cupertino, California, founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak. It makes the iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch and AirPods and earns from services such as the App Store, iCloud and Apple Music.
aave: Aave is one of the largest decentralized lending protocols, where users lend and borrow crypto without intermediaries. It runs on Ethereum and many other networks; the AAVE token is used for governance and to backstop the protocol. Its founder is Stani Kulechov.
abbn: ABB is a Swiss-Swedish engineering company based in Zurich, formed in 1988 by merging Sweden's ASEA and Switzerland's Brown Boveri. It makes electrification equipment, electric motors, industrial automation and EV charging stations.
abbv: AbbVie is an American biopharmaceutical company based in North Chicago, Illinois, spun off from Abbott Laboratories in 2013. It is known for the immunology drugs Humira, Skyrizi and Rinvoq and, since buying Allergan, also for Botox.
abey: ABEYCHAIN (ABEY) is a layered, programmable blockchain designed for high transaction volumes that also offers decentralized data storage. The ABEY token is used to pay fees and run applications on the network.
abt: Abbott Laboratories is an American healthcare company based in Illinois, founded in 1888. It makes medical devices (including FreeStyle Libre glucose monitors), diagnostic tests, Similac infant formula and Ensure nutrition drinks, and generic medicines.
acn: Accenture is a global consulting and IT services company legally domiciled in Dublin, Ireland. It helps businesses and governments with digital transformation, cloud, cybersecurity and AI adoption, and runs entire business processes as an outsourcer.
acu: Acurast (ACU) is a decentralized compute network that uses ordinary smartphones instead of data centers. Phone owners contribute processing power to run apps, APIs and AI models and earn rewards, while developers get verifiable confidential computing.
acx: Across Protocol (ACX) is a bridge for moving assets quickly between Ethereum and layer-2 networks, secured by UMA's optimistic oracle. Independent relayers complete transfers almost instantly, and ACX serves as the governance token.
ada: Cardano is a smart-contract blockchain developed on the basis of peer-reviewed academic research. It was founded by Ethereum co-founder Charles Hoskinson, runs on the Ouroboros proof-of-stake protocol, and ADA is used for fees, staking and governance.
adi: Analog Devices is an American maker of analog and mixed-signal chips based in Massachusetts, founded in 1965. Its chips convert real-world signals such as sound, temperature and motion into digital data and back, and are used in industry, cars, communications and medicine.
adi-token: ADI (ADI Chain) is an Ethereum layer-2 network from the Abu Dhabi-based ADI Foundation, aimed at government and enterprise infrastructure. Built on ZKsync's ZK Stack, it lets countries and companies run systems for payments, e-invoicing and registries.
aero: Aero is a decentralized exchange and liquidity hub in the Ethereum ecosystem that grew out of Aerodrome, the popular DEX on Base. Users swap tokens, earn rewards for providing liquidity and launch new assets, while token holders vote on how emissions are distributed.
agg: iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond (AGG) is BlackRock's ETF on the broad US investment-grade bond market, from government to corporate debt.
agricultural-bank-of-china: Agricultural Bank of China is one of China's four big state-owned banks, headquartered in Beijing and founded in 1951. It has one of the widest branch networks in the country, including villages and small towns, and lends to farmers and the agricultural sector.
ain: Infinity Ground is blockchain infrastructure for "vibe coders", where anyone can create and own decentralized apps using natural language and AI agents. AIN is the ecosystem token.
aioz: AIOZ Network (AIOZ) is a DePIN network for data storage, video streaming and AI computing. Participants share their computers' resources as network nodes and earn AIOZ tokens, which are also used to pay for the network's services.
air: Airbus is a European aerospace group headquartered in Leiden with main plants in Toulouse and Hamburg, founded in 1970. It is one of the world's two biggest makers of passenger jets, such as the A320 and A350, and also builds helicopters, military aircraft and satellites.
ake: AKEDO is a multi-agent AI platform for automatic content creation: users can build simple games in minutes just by describing them in plain language. The platform runs on large language models; AKE is the ecosystem token.
akt: Akash Network is a decentralized cloud computing marketplace built with the Cosmos SDK, where server owners rent out CPU and GPU capacity. It is a cheaper alternative to AWS or Google Cloud that is popular for AI workloads; AKT is used for payments and staking.
alch: Alchemist AI (ALCH) is a no-code platform that builds software from a plain-text description, so users don't need to program. People generate games, websites and tools with AI, and the ALCH token gives access to platform features.
aleo: Aleo (ALEO) is a layer-1 blockchain for private applications, where smart contracts run with zero-knowledge proofs. User data stays hidden while the network only verifies that computations are correct; ALEO is used for fees and rewards.
algo: Algorand is a blockchain for smart contracts and payments founded by MIT professor and Turing Award winner Silvio Micali. Its Pure Proof of Stake consensus gives fast transaction finality; ALGO pays fees and is used to take part in consensus.
alibaba: Alibaba Group is a Chinese technology company based in Hangzhou, founded by Jack Ma in 1999. It runs China's largest online marketplaces Taobao and Tmall, the international store AliExpress, the cloud business Alibaba Cloud and the logistics network Cainiao.
allo: Allora (ALLO) is a decentralized AI network that brings together many specialized models and combines their forecasts into one more accurate result. Anyone can contribute a model, data or verification; AI agents and DeFi apps use the outputs in real time.
alt: AltLayer (ALT) is a protocol for quickly launching custom rollup blockchains (optimistic and zk) on a «rollup-as-a-service» basis. It uses restaking through EigenLayer for extra network security; ALT is used for staking and governance.
aluminum: Aluminium is a light metal used in aircraft, cars, packaging and construction. Producing it takes huge amounts of electricity, so its price also depends on energy costs.
alv: Allianz is Europe's largest insurance company, based in Munich and founded in 1890. It sells property, car and life insurance in more than 70 countries and manages huge investment funds through PIMCO and Allianz Global Investors.
amat: Applied Materials is the world's largest supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, founded in 1967 and based in Santa Clara, California. Its machines deposit and process layers of material on silicon wafers for TSMC, Samsung, Intel and other chipmakers.
amd: AMD (Advanced Micro Devices) is a US chip designer from Santa Clara, California, founded in 1969. It makes Ryzen and EPYC processors, Radeon graphics cards and Instinct AI accelerators, plus chips for PlayStation and Xbox consoles; it is led by Lisa Su.
amgn: Amgen is one of the world's largest biotech companies, based in Thousand Oaks, California, and founded in 1980. It develops medicines for osteoporosis, cancer, inflammatory and cardiovascular diseases, including Enbrel, Prolia and Repatha.
amp-token: Amp (AMP) is an Ethereum token that serves as digital collateral for instant, guaranteed payments. It is used by the Flexa payment network: while a blockchain transaction confirms, AMP collateral guarantees that the merchant gets paid.
amzn: Amazon is a US company based in Seattle, founded by Jeff Bezos in 1994 as an online bookstore. Today it runs a huge online store, the AWS cloud, Prime subscriptions, Prime Video streaming and the Alexa voice assistant.
anet: Arista Networks is a US networking-equipment maker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 2004 with Andy Bechtolsheim among its founders. It supplies high-speed switches and its EOS software for data centers and AI cloud clusters at major tech companies.
ankr: Ankr (ANKR) is a provider of decentralized Web3 infrastructure: it gives developers access to nodes of dozens of blockchains via RPC and offers liquid staking services. The ANKR token is used to pay for services and for staking.
antfun: ANT.FUN is a Web3 social trading wallet that works with several major blockchains. It combines a wallet, on-chain analytics, tracking of other wallets, trading signals and trader chats, so users can find and execute trades in one app.
anvl: Anvil (ANVL) is a set of Ethereum smart contracts that manage collateral and issue fully secured credit, such as letters of credit — a digital version of a bank cheque backed by verified funds. This reduces counterparty risk; ANVL is the protocol's token.
ape: ApeCoin (APE) is a token linked to the Bored Ape Yacht Club NFT collection by Yuga Labs, launched in 2022. It is used in games and projects across the ecosystem, holders vote in ApeCoin DAO, and it powers its own network, ApeChain.
apepe: Ape and Pepe (APEPE) is a meme coin that combines two popular meme figures, an ape and Pepe the frog, as a symbol of small retail investors. It has no technological function and relies solely on community activity.
apex: ApeX Protocol is a decentralized exchange for trading perpetual futures, spot, tokenized stocks and prediction markets while keeping control of your own assets. The project is backed by the Bybit exchange; APEX is the governance and rewards token.
aph: Amphenol is an American maker of electronic and fiber-optic connectors, cables and sensors based in Connecticut, founded in 1932. Its components are used in data centers, cars, aircraft, military equipment and mobile devices.
api3: Api3 (API3) is an oracle project in which price data for DeFi is signed by the API providers themselves rather than by middlemen. Its OEV mechanism returns part of the profit from liquidations to apps, and the API3 token is used for staking and DAO governance.
apt: Aptos is a proof-of-stake layer-1 blockchain created by former developers of Meta's Diem project. It uses the Move programming language and executes transactions in parallel; APT pays network fees and secures the chain through staking.
ar: Arweave is a decentralized network for permanent data storage: you pay once and the file is meant to be stored "forever" on what it calls the permaweb. The project was founded by Sam Williams; the AO computing platform also runs on Arweave, and AR pays for storage.
arb: Arbitrum is the largest layer-2 network for Ethereum, developed by Offchain Labs. Its optimistic rollup technology makes transactions much cheaper and faster while keeping Ethereum's security; ARB is the ecosystem's governance token.
arc: AI Rig Complex (ARC) is a Solana project that develops Rig, a Rust framework for building AI agents and apps powered by large language models. The ARC token is used by the project's community.
aria: Aria.AI (ARIA) is an experimental game development and publishing project that combines AI technology and the idea of Disney-style immersive worlds with its own intellectual property. The ARIA token is used within the project's ecosystem.
ark: ARK is a blockchain project launched in 2017 that provides tools for building your own blockchains and linking them together. Its aim is a web of connected networks, and the ARK token is used for fees and for voting for delegates who secure the network.
arkk: ARK Innovation (ARKK) is an actively managed fund run by Cathie Wood's ARK Invest that bets on 'disruptive' technologies such as AI, genomics and fintech. It is very volatile.
arkm: Arkham (ARKM) is a blockchain analytics platform that uses AI to link anonymous addresses to real companies and people, and it also runs its own crypto exchange. Users track the flows of big players; ARKM is used for rewards and fee discounts.
arm: Arm Holdings is a British company based in Cambridge, founded in 1990. It designs processor architectures and licenses them to chipmakers; almost every smartphone in the world runs on Arm designs. SoftBank owns a controlling stake.
asml: ASML is a Dutch company from Veldhoven and the world's only maker of EUV lithography machines, which are needed to produce the most advanced microchips. TSMC, Samsung and Intel buy its equipment; it was founded in 1984 as a joint venture of Philips and ASM International.
asml-etf: ASML is a Dutch company based in Veldhoven, founded in 1984, and the only maker of EUV lithography machines in the world. The most advanced microchips cannot be made without its equipment, so its customers include TSMC, Samsung and Intel.
asset: REAL (ASSET) is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain built specifically for tokenizing, insuring and trading real-world financial assets. The token powers the network, whose goal is to bring traditional finance on-chain.
aster: Aster is a decentralized perpetual futures exchange (perp DEX) running mainly on BNB Chain and other networks. It combines trading without handing funds to an exchange with features of professional platforms; ASTER is the governance and rewards token.
astr: Astar (ASTR) is a blockchain ecosystem founded by Japanese entrepreneur Sota Watanabe. It started as a Polkadot parachain and later expanded to Soneium, an Ethereum network; the project is popular in Japan and works with large corporations, and ASTR is its main token.
ath: Aethir (ATH) is a decentralized GPU cloud for companies that need powerful graphics processors for artificial intelligence and cloud gaming. Hardware owners rent out their GPUs to the network and clients lease them; ATH is used for payments and staking.
atom: Cosmos is an ecosystem of independent blockchains linked by the IBC protocol, which lets them exchange data and tokens. Dozens of networks are built with its tools (Cosmos SDK, CometBFT); ATOM is used for staking and governance of the Cosmos Hub.
auki: Auki is a project that makes the physical world accessible to AI, robots and smart glasses. Its posemesh protocol gives devices a shared spatial understanding so they can navigate and find information inside real buildings; AUKI is the network's token.
aurora: Aurora is an Ethereum-compatible virtual machine (EVM) built on the NEAR Protocol blockchain. It lets developers run Ethereum apps with high throughput and low fees; the AURORA token is used for governance.
auto: Hastra AUTO is a token that gives exposure to the yield of a pool of US consumer auto loans on Figure's Democratized Prime platform. Holders earn the interest paid by real car-loan borrowers, minus the Hastra platform fee.
avax: Avalanche is a smart-contract platform developed by Ava Labs, led by Emin Gün Sirer. It lets teams launch their own blockchains (L1s) for games, finance and business; AVAX pays fees and is used for staking.
avgo: Broadcom is a US company from Palo Alto, California, that designs semiconductors for networking, data centers, smartphones and custom AI accelerators for big tech companies. Since buying VMware, it is also a major supplier of enterprise software.
avnt: Veranta (AVNT) is a decentralized perpetual futures exchange on the Base network where people can trade not only crypto but also real-world assets such as currencies, commodities and stocks. The AVNT token is used for governance and incentives.
awe: AWE Network is a project building identity and payment infrastructure for the AI agent economy. It began as the Autonomous World Engine, an engine for multi-agent worlds where many agents act at once; AWE is the ecosystem's governance token.
axl: Axelar (AXL) is a cross-chain network that passes messages and assets between dozens of blockchains, including Ethereum, Cosmos and Solana. Developers use a simple API to build apps that work on several networks at once; AXL is used for validator staking and fees.
axp: American Express is a US payments company based in New York, founded in 1850. It issues Amex credit and charge cards, processes the transactions itself and lends to cardholders, and is known for its rewards programs and travel services for affluent customers.
axs: Axie Infinity (AXS) is the governance token of Axie Infinity, a game by Vietnamese studio Sky Mavis in which players collect and battle fantasy NFT creatures. The game became a symbol of the 2021 play-to-earn boom and runs on the Ronin network.
azn-etf: AstraZeneca is a British-Swedish pharmaceutical company based in Cambridge, formed in 1999 by the merger of Astra and Zeneca. It develops medicines for cancer, cardiovascular and respiratory diseases and is known for the COVID-19 vaccine developed with Oxford.
aztec: Aztec is a privacy-focused layer-2 network on Ethereum: developers build apps in which users' transactions and data can be hidden using zero-knowledge proofs. The London-based team created its own programming language, Noir.
b: BUILDon (B) is a meme token on BNB Chain that emerged around the USD1 stablecoin and the community of "builders" in its ecosystem. Its value rests on community interest and trading rather than on a specific product.
b3: B3 is a project created by former members of the Base team that builds infrastructure for games, AI agents and automated workflows that execute on-chain transactions. Its main product, B3OS, is a workflow automation platform for agents.
ba: Boeing is an American aerospace giant founded in Seattle in 1916 by William Boeing. It builds the 737, 777 and 787 passenger jets, military aircraft, satellites and space systems, and services airline fleets worldwide.
baby: Babylon (BABY) is a protocol that lets bitcoin holders stake BTC to secure other proof-of-stake blockchains without bridges or custodians, while the coins stay on the Bitcoin network. It was founded by Stanford researchers including David Tse; BABY is the token of Babylon's own chain.
babydoge: Baby Doge Coin (BABYDOGE) is a memecoin on BNB Chain launched in 2021 as the «child» of Dogecoin. Part of every transaction is burned and part is distributed to holders; the community is also known for charity work supporting animal shelters.
bac: Bank of America is one of the largest banks in the United States, headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. It serves millions of individual and business customers and runs an investment bank and the Merrill brokerage; Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway is one of its biggest shareholders.
ban: Comedian (BAN) is a meme token on Solana inspired by Maurizio Cattelan's controversial artwork «Comedian» — a banana duct-taped to a wall that sold at auction for millions of dollars in 2024.
bananas31: Banana For Scale (BANANAS31) is a memecoin on BNB Chain inspired by a 2012 Reddit meme in which a banana is placed next to an object «for scale». It is a community token with no practical function whose price depends on interest in the meme.
band: Band Protocol (BAND) is a decentralized oracle founded in Thailand in 2017 that delivers outside data such as prices to blockchains and AI apps. It runs on its own BandChain blockchain in the Cosmos ecosystem.
bank-of-china: Bank of China is one of China's four big state-owned banks, headquartered in Beijing and founded in 1912. The most international of Chinese banks, it specializes in foreign-exchange and trade finance and has branches in dozens of countries.
bard: Lombard (BARD) is a protocol founded in 2024 that turns bitcoin into a yield-earning asset in DeFi. Users stake BTC through Babylon and receive LBTC, a liquid token that works across many blockchains; BARD is the governance token.
bas-token: BNB Attestation Service (BAS) is a protocol for creating on-chain attestations on BNB Chain: verified records about identity, reputation or events that other apps can rely on. The BAS token is used within the service's ecosystem.
bat: Basic Attention Token (BAT) is the token of the ad ecosystem of the Brave browser, created by Brendan Eich, the inventor of JavaScript and co-founder of Mozilla. Advertisers pay in BAT, and users who opt in to private ads get a share they can use to support websites and creators.
bbva: BBVA is Spain's second-largest bank, headquartered in Bilbao and Madrid. The group's biggest business is Mexico's BBVA México; it also controls Turkey's Garanti BBVA, operates in South America and is known for its advanced digital banking.
bch: Bitcoin Cash is a cryptocurrency that split off from bitcoin in a 2017 hard fork. Its supporters raised the block size so the network can handle more transactions with lower fees, promoting BCH as digital cash for everyday payments.
bdx-token: Beldex is a privacy cryptocurrency and ecosystem launched in 2018. The BDX coin enables private transfers, and the project builds data-protection tools including the BChat messenger, a browser and a private VPN.
beam: Beam is a blockchain gaming ecosystem that grew out of the Merit Circle gaming guild and runs as its own network on Avalanche. It gives game studios infrastructure for games, NFTs and other digital products; BEAM is the native token used for transaction fees in the network.
bera: Berachain (BERA) is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain using a Proof of Liquidity mechanism, which grew out of the community around the Bong Bears NFT collection. BERA is the gas token used to pay fees, while a separate token, BGT, handles governance and rewards.
bfc: Bifrost (BFC) is a South Korean blockchain project building a multichain network and bridges for decentralized apps that run across different blockchains. The BFC token pays for network services and is used for staking.
bfusd: BFUSD is a reward-bearing margin asset created by Binance for its futures traders, launched in 2024. Users swap USDT for BFUSD, use it as collateral for futures positions and receive daily rewards generated by Binance's yield strategies; it is not an independent on-chain stablecoin.
bhartiartl: Bharti Airtel is an Indian telecom operator based in New Delhi, founded by Sunil Mittal in 1995. One of the world's largest mobile operators, it works in India and many African countries (Airtel Africa) and also provides broadband and TV.
bhp: BHP is an Australian mining company based in Melbourne, one of the largest in the world, with a history dating back to 1885. It mines iron ore, copper and metallurgical coal and is developing a potash project in Canada.
bio: Bio Protocol (BIO) is a decentralized science (DeSci) protocol that helps communities of patients and scientists fund biotech research and own the rights to it. The project was backed by Binance Labs, and BIO is used for governance and to support BioDAOs.
bless: Bless Network (BLESS) is a San Francisco-based decentralized computing platform that turns the spare capacity of everyday devices such as laptops and phones into a shared global computer. Participants earn tokens for the computing power they provide.
blk: BlackRock is the world's largest investment manager, headquartered in New York and founded in 1988 by Larry Fink. It manages pension and investment money, issues ETFs under the iShares brand, including the bitcoin fund IBIT, and built the Aladdin risk-analytics platform.
blkgrwon: Ondo High Growth Powered by BlackRock (BLKGRWON) is a tokenized investment portfolio from Ondo Finance aimed at long-term capital growth. It holds roughly 95% stocks through BlackRock's iShares equity strategies across US and international markets, plus about 5% in bitcoin.
bnb: BNB is the coin of the BNB Chain ecosystem, launched in 2017 by the Binance exchange founded by Changpeng Zhao. It pays fees on BNB Smart Chain, gives trading-fee discounts on Binance and is used in DeFi and staking.
bnd: Vanguard Total Bond Market (BND) covers the whole US investment-grade bond market in one fund: Treasuries, corporate bonds and mortgage-backed securities.
bnkr: BankrCoin (BNKR) is the official token of Bankr, an AI agent that buys and sells crypto through ordinary chat messages. Bankr is known for helping users of the Farcaster social network buy coins right in their feed.
bnt: Bancor is an ecosystem of decentralized protocols for on-chain trading and liquidity, launched in 2017. Bancor was one of the pioneers of automated market makers (AMMs), and its Carbon protocol lets users set up automatic trading strategies; BNT is used for governance.
bome: BOOK OF MEME (BOME) is a meme token on Solana created in 2024 by the artist Darkfarms. It was conceived as a decentralized digital archive of memes stored on Arweave and IPFS, and became known for its rapid surge right after launch.
bonk: Bonk is a dog-themed meme coin on Solana, launched on Christmas 2022 to cheer up the community after the FTX collapse. A large share of the tokens was given away free to Solana users and developers, and BONK is integrated into many apps on the network.
bora: BORA is a blockchain platform for games and digital entertainment created by a South Korean company that belongs to the Kakao group. It distributes games and digital content and rewards participants with BORA tokens.
bp: Backpack is a crypto exchange and wallet in one app, founded by Armani Ferrante's team, which previously built developer tools for Solana. The exchange offers spot and futures trading, and the wallet supports several blockchains; BP is the ecosystem token.
br-token: Bedrock (BR) is a liquid restaking protocol that issues liquid tokens such as uniBTC and uniETH for staked BTC, ETH and other assets. BR is the governance token: holders lock it as veBR to vote on protocol settings and on how rewards are split between liquidity pools.
brent: Brent is the world's main benchmark for crude oil, named after a North Sea field. Most of the oil traded globally is priced off Brent.
brett: Brett (BRETT) is a meme token on Coinbase's Base network, named after a character from Matt Furie's Boy's Club comic, a friend of Pepe the Frog. The community promotes it as «the Pepe of Base».
brk-b: Berkshire Hathaway is an American conglomerate from Omaha, Nebraska, led for decades by Warren Buffett. It owns the insurer GEICO, the BNSF railroad, energy companies and Duracell, and holds large stakes in Apple, Coca-Cola and American Express.
bsv: Bitcoin SV (Satoshi Vision) is a cryptocurrency that split off from Bitcoin Cash in a 2018 hard fork. Its backers, including Craig Wright, pushed for very large blocks to scale, and the network positions itself as a platform for micropayments and enterprise data.
btc: Bitcoin is the first cryptocurrency, launched in 2009 by the pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto. Its supply is capped at 21 million coins, which is why it is often called 'digital gold'.
btw: BTW is the utility and governance token of the Bitway ecosystem, which offers yield, payments and financing services. The token is used for staking, voting and running the network, tying all Bitway products together.
bx: Blackstone is the world's largest alternative asset manager, founded in New York in 1985 by Stephen Schwarzman and Peter Peterson. It invests in private equity, real estate, credit and hedge funds on behalf of pension funds and other investors.
c: Citigroup is one of the largest US banks, headquartered in New York, with a history dating back to 1812. Citi serves corporations, governments and individuals in nearly a hundred countries with payments, credit cards, investment banking and wealth management.
cake: PancakeSwap is a decentralized exchange (DEX) launched in 2020 on BNB Chain, where it became the most popular one. Users swap tokens, provide liquidity, farm and play lotteries; CAKE is the reward and governance token.
cap: Cap is a covered-credit protocol on Ethereum built around the digital dollar cUSD, which is backed by dollar assets such as money market funds and regulated stablecoins. Reserves are lent to institutions to earn yield, and each loan is protected by a separate market of financial guarantees.
cards: Collector Crypt is a platform that tokenizes physical trading cards, mainly Pokémon: the cards sit in a vault while the token holder owns them. Users can buy, sell or open digital card packs, and CARDS is the platform's token on Solana.
cat: Caterpillar is the world's largest maker of construction and mining equipment, founded in 1925 and headquartered in Irving, Texas. It is known for yellow bulldozers, excavators and mining trucks and also builds diesel engines, gas turbines and locomotives.
cati: Catizen is a cat-themed social game in Telegram built on the TON blockchain. It makes it easier for millions of messenger users to get into Web3 and mobile payments, and CATI is the game ecosystem's token.
catl: CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology) is a Chinese battery maker from Ningde in Fujian province, founded in 2011 by Robin Zeng. It is the world's biggest supplier of electric-vehicle batteries, serving carmakers such as Tesla, BMW and Volkswagen, and also makes energy-storage systems.
cattle: Live cattle is a futures contract that tracks the price of beef cattle in the United States. It depends on feed costs, herd size and demand for meat.
cb: Chubb is one of the world's largest property and casualty insurers, headquartered in Zurich, Switzerland. It insures businesses, individuals and farmers and also offers reinsurance, life and health insurance in dozens of countries.
cba: Commonwealth Bank of Australia is Australia's largest bank, based in Sydney and founded in 1911 as a state bank. It serves individuals and businesses, is known for its mobile banking app and also owns ASB Bank in New Zealand.
cc: Canton Coin (CC) is the native token of Canton Network, a blockchain for banks and financial institutions built by the company Digital Asset. The network combines data privacy with the ability to exchange tokenised assets, and CC rewards developers, users and infrastructure operators for real activity.
ccd: Concordium (CCD) is a layer-1 blockchain founded in Switzerland by Danish entrepreneur Lars Seier Christensen, with identity verification built into the protocol. This combines privacy with regulatory compliance and can confirm that actions, including those of AI agents, were authorized by a real person.
celo: Celo (CELO) is a blockchain launched in 2020 for mobile payments that became a layer-2 network on Ethereum in 2025. It is known for cheap stablecoin transfers, especially for users in developing countries.
cent: Incentiv is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain with built-in account abstraction, which makes wallets and fee payments simpler. The network shares revenue with users and developers for their activity, and CENT is its native token.
cfg-token: Centrifuge (CFG) is a protocol for tokenizing real-world assets such as loans, invoices and Treasury bonds, founded in Berlin in 2017. It gives investors access to these assets in DeFi, and CFG is the governance token.
cfx: Conflux is a public Layer 1 blockchain founded in China that uses a hybrid Tree-Graph consensus and is compatible with Ethereum apps (EVM). It is known for working with Chinese companies and public bodies; CFX pays network fees and is used for staking.
cheems: Cheems Token (CHEEMS) is a memecoin on BNB Chain inspired by the famous meme of a Shiba Inu dog named Cheems. It is a community token with no utility that exists thanks to the meme's popularity and its holders' enthusiasm.
china-construction-bank: China Construction Bank is one of China's "Big Four" state-owned banks, headquartered in Beijing and founded in 1954. It offers corporate and retail banking and has historically specialised in financing infrastructure, construction and mortgages.
china-merchants-bank: China Merchants Bank is a Chinese commercial bank from Shenzhen, founded in 1987. It is regarded as a leader in China's retail banking, known for its credit cards, mobile app and wealth management for affluent clients.
china-mobile: China Mobile is China's state-owned telecom operator and the world's largest mobile carrier by number of subscribers. It provides mobile service, home broadband, cloud and enterprise services; the company was created in 1997.
china-shenhua-energy: China Shenhua Energy is China's largest coal company and a subsidiary of state-owned China Energy Investment. It runs an integrated model: it mines coal, moves it on its own railways and through its ports, and burns it to generate electricity at its own power plants.
chz: Chiliz (CHZ) is a Malta-based sports blockchain that powers the Socios.com app. Clubs such as Barcelona, PSG and Juventus issue fan tokens on it that let supporters vote in club polls and get perks; CHZ is the currency of this ecosystem.
ckb: Nervos Network (CKB) is a layered blockchain network launched in 2019 by a Chinese team. Its layer 1, the Common Knowledge Base, acts as a secure foundation for storing value, while fast transactions move to layer 2. CKB pays for storage space on the chain and is mined.
clear: Clearpool (CLEAR) is a DeFi credit marketplace where lenders deposit stablecoins into on-chain vaults that fund vetted institutional borrowers such as trading firms and fintechs. Each vault has a risk curator who checks borrowers and monitors repayments; Ripple has backed its expansion to the XRP Ledger.
coai: ChainOpera AI (COAI) is a platform for jointly building AI agents that are governed and owned by the community. It combines a «super AI» app with infrastructure for developers; the COAI token is used for incentives and governance.
coco: COCO is a memecoin with no specific technical function, built around the image of a 'discovered' meme that keeps moving forward without stopping. Its value rests on its community and internet culture rather than on a product or revenue.
cocoa: Cocoa is the raw material for chocolate. Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana grow more than half of the world's crop, so tree diseases and weather there move the price strongly.
coffee: Coffee is one of the most traded agricultural commodities. The benchmark contract is arabica, and prices depend on harvests and weather in Brazil, Vietnam and Colombia.
coindepo: COINDEPO is a platform that combines interest-bearing deposit accounts for crypto assets with instant crypto loans. The COINDEPO token gives higher rates and discounts within the service; like any yield service, it carries platform risk.
comp: Compound is one of the first decentralized lending protocols on Ethereum, launched in 2018 by Robert Leshner's team. Users earn interest on deposited crypto or borrow against collateral; COMP is the governance token, and its 2020 distribution helped spark the DeFi boom.
cop: ConocoPhillips is one of the largest independent US oil and gas companies, based in Houston and focused on exploration and production. It produces crude oil, natural gas and liquefied natural gas in the United States, Canada, Norway, Australia and other countries.
copper: Copper is the key metal of electrification: wires, electric motors, EVs, power grids and data centres all need it. Its price is often seen as a gauge of the global economy.
corn: Corn (maize) is the world's biggest grain crop by volume: livestock feed, food ingredient and ethanol biofuel. The United States is the top producer.
cost: Costco is an American chain of membership-only warehouse stores headquartered in Issaquah, Washington, founded in 1983. It sells groceries, household goods and electronics in bulk at low prices and is known for its own brand, Kirkland Signature.
coti: COTI is an Ethereum-based network that brings data privacy to a public blockchain using the Garbled Circuits cryptographic protocol. It lets smart contracts process encrypted data; the COTI token pays fees and is used for staking.
cotton: Cotton is the main natural fibre for clothing and textiles. The biggest producers are China, India, the United States and Brazil.
cow: CoW Protocol (COW) is a DeFi token-swap protocol on Ethereum and other chains that grew out of Gnosis. It batches orders, matches opposite trades directly and protects users from MEV attacks; COW is used for governance via CowDAO.
crm: Salesforce is a US company from San Francisco, founded in 1999 by Marc Benioff and a pioneer of cloud software. It leads the market for CRM systems used for sales, customer service and marketing, and also owns Slack and Tableau.
cro: Cronos is an Ethereum-compatible (EVM) blockchain built on the Cosmos SDK and closely tied to the Crypto.com platform. CRO pays network fees and unlocks perks in the Crypto.com app and on its cards.
crv: Curve Finance is a decentralized exchange launched in 2020 by Michael Egorov that specializes in swapping assets with similar prices, such as stablecoins, with minimal slippage. CRV is the governance and reward token for liquidity providers.
crwd: CrowdStrike is an American cybersecurity company based in Austin, Texas, founded in 2011 by George Kurtz. Its cloud platform Falcon protects companies' computers, servers and cloud systems from hackers; a faulty update in July 2024 caused a worldwide Windows outage.
csco: Cisco is an American company from San Jose, California, founded in 1984 and one of the world's largest makers of networking equipment. It sells routers, switches and cybersecurity products, runs the Webex video platform and bought the data analytics firm Splunk in 2024.
cspr: Casper Network (CSPR) is a Proof of Stake layer-1 blockchain launched in March 2021. It targets businesses and the tokenization of real-world assets and supports upgradeable smart contracts; CSPR is used for fees and staking.
ct: Concrete is a DeFi protocol with automated vaults that place users' crypto assets into yield strategies. It makes DeFi yield easier to access for both ordinary and institutional investors; CT is the protocol's token.
ctc: Creditcoin (CTC) is a blockchain built to record credit histories and loans, especially in emerging markets. It is developed by the South Korean team Gluwa; the CTC token is used for fees and staking on the network.
ctr: Citrea is the first ZK rollup that settles directly on Bitcoin, verifying zero-knowledge proofs through BitVM. It adds full smart contracts to Bitcoin via its own zkEVM while keeping Bitcoin-level security.
cvx: Chevron is one of the largest US oil and gas companies, headquartered in Houston, Texas, with roots going back to 1879 and Standard Oil. It produces oil and gas, refines them at its own plants and sells fuel under the Chevron, Texaco and Caltex brands.
cvx-token: Convex Finance (CVX) is a DeFi protocol on Ethereum built on top of Curve, the stablecoin exchange. It lets Curve liquidity providers earn boosted rewards without locking CRV tokens themselves; CVX holders influence how those rewards are distributed.
dai: Dai (DAI) is a decentralized stablecoin pegged to the US dollar, launched in 2017 by MakerDAO (now Sky). Users mint DAI by locking more crypto than they borrow in smart contracts, so no bank holds the reserves; it is widely used in Ethereum DeFi.
dash-token: Dash is a cryptocurrency for fast, cheap payments, launched in 2014 by Evan Duffield (first as XCoin, then Darkcoin). Its network uses masternodes for instant InstantSend transfers and its own funding and governance system.
data: Data Network (DATA) is a layer-1 blockchain built to register intellectual property rights for data used in AI. It lets owners record rights to datasets on-chain and earn from them, and the DATA token is used inside the network.
dbr: deBridge (DBR) is a cross-chain protocol for moving assets and data quickly between blockchains, including Solana and EVM networks, without its own liquidity pools. Its DLN service executes swaps between networks in seconds; DBR is used for governance and rewards.
dcr: Decred is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 with hybrid consensus: miners create blocks (Proof of Work), while DCR holders who stake their coins validate them and vote on changes. This way the community itself governs the network, and part of new issuance funds its development.
de: Deere & Company is a US maker of agricultural and construction machinery based in Illinois, founded in 1837 by John Deere. It is known for its green John Deere tractors and combines and for precision-farming technology.
deep: DeepBook (DEEP) is the native decentralized order book of the Sui network, launched in July 2023 with support from Mysten Labs and the Sui Foundation. Exchanges and DeFi apps on Sui use it for trading, and the DEEP token gives fee discounts and voting rights.
degen: Degen (DEGEN) is a community token of the Base network that appeared in 2024 among users of the Farcaster social network. It is used to tip content creators and active members, and the project later launched its own Degen Chain.
dell: Dell Technologies is an American computer maker based in Round Rock, Texas, founded in 1984 by Michael Dell in his college dorm room. It sells Dell, XPS and Alienware laptops and PCs as well as servers, data storage and infrastructure for AI data centers.
dep: DEAPCOIN (DEP) is the token of the Japanese gaming platform PlayMining, run by Singapore-based Digital Entertainment Asset. Users earn DEP by playing free games and enjoying manga and anime content, and can use it to buy NFTs.
dexe: DeXe (DEXE) is a protocol for creating and running decentralized autonomous organizations (DAOs). It offers ready-made tools for voting, treasuries and delegation, and the DEXE token is used to govern the platform itself.
dgai: DGrid AI (DGAI) is a decentralized AI infrastructure network that gives access to many AI models through a single OpenAI-compatible gateway. The network routes requests between model providers and node operators and settles payments for their services.
dhr: Danaher is a US science and technology conglomerate from Washington, D.C., founded in 1969 by brothers Steven and Mitchell Rales. It makes diagnostic equipment, biotechnology tools and lab systems under brands such as Beckman Coulter, Cepheid, Leica Biosystems and Cytiva.
dia: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average (DIA) is an ETF on the Dow Jones index: 30 of the best-known large US companies, weighted by share price.
dis: The Walt Disney Company is an American media and entertainment company based in Burbank, California, founded in 1923 by Walt and Roy Disney. It owns the Disney, Pixar, Marvel and Lucasfilm studios, the Disney+ streaming service, the ABC and ESPN networks, and theme parks around the world.
dna: NeoSoul is a project building market infrastructure for the AI-agent economy, where agents learn, compete, coordinate and create measurable value. DNA is the ecosystem token.
dodo: DODO is a decentralized exchange on Ethereum, BNB Chain and other networks that uses its own Proactive Market Maker (PMM) algorithm with oracle prices. It aims to let users trade with less price slippage, and DODO is its governance token.
dog: Dog (Bitcoin), or DOG•GO•TO•THE•MOON, is a memecoin native to the Bitcoin blockchain, issued in 2024 under the Runes standard. Tokens were airdropped to holders of a rare-sat artifact with no team sale, and it is pitched as a way to bring new people to Bitcoin.
doge: Dogecoin is the first famous memecoin, created in 2013 by Billy Markus and Jackson Palmer as a joke based on the Shiba Inu dog meme. It is used for payments and tipping, and Elon Musk's posts boosted its fame.
dos: DAPPOS (DOS) is a protocol that simplifies using blockchains through «intents»: the user only states what they want to do, and the network finds the way to execute it across different blockchains. DOS is the token of this ecosystem.
dot: Polkadot is a multi-chain network that joins separate blockchains into one system with cross-chain messaging and shared security. It was created by Ethereum co-founder Gavin Wood; DOT is used for staking, governance and paying for network resources.
drv: Derive (formerly Lyra) is a decentralized protocol for options, perpetual futures and structured products, running on its own Derive Chain built on the OP Stack. DRV is the governance token: holders steer the protocol and receive a share of fee revenue.
dte-de: Deutsche Telekom is Europe's largest telecom company, based in Bonn, and the former state postal and telephone network of Germany. It provides mobile and internet services in Germany and across Europe and controls the US operator T-Mobile US.
dusk: Dusk (DUSK) is a layer-1 blockchain from the Netherlands built for regulated financial markets. It lets tokenized securities be issued and traded in line with EU law while protecting privacy; DUSK is used for fees and staking.
dydx: dYdX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures, founded in 2017 by former Coinbase engineer Antonio Juliano. It now runs on its own blockchain in the Cosmos ecosystem; the DYDX token is used for staking, network security and governance.
edu: Open Campus (EDU) is a protocol building blockchain infrastructure for education: digital diplomas and certificates and funding for educational content. The project is backed by Animoca Brands and runs its own network, EDU Chain.
eem: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets (EEM) is a BlackRock ETF holding large companies from emerging markets, including China, India and Taiwan.
efa: iShares MSCI EAFE (EFA) invests in large companies from Europe, Australasia and the Far East, excluding the US and Canada.
egld: MultiversX (formerly Elrond) is a layer-1 blockchain from Romania that uses sharding for high throughput. Launched in 2020, it supports smart contracts and DeFi; EGLD pays fees and is used for staking and governance.
eigen: EigenCloud (formerly EigenLayer) is a restaking protocol on Ethereum: staked ETH is reused to secure other services and networks. The project was founded by Sreeram Kannan, and the EIGEN token is used for governance and to back guarantees for its verifiable cloud services.
elf: aelf (ELF) is a layer-1 blockchain from Singapore, launched in 2017, built with a main chain and side chains for scaling. Smart contracts are written in C#, and the project focuses on AI tools for developers.
ena: Ethena is an Ethereum protocol that issues USDe, a synthetic dollar kept stable by crypto collateral and hedging with futures. ENA is the protocol's governance token; the project was founded by Guy Young.
enj: Enjin Coin (ENJ) is the token of the Enjin ecosystem, which has been building infrastructure for in-game NFT items since 2017. Developers issue in-game objects on Enjin's own blockchain, and ENJ is used to create them, pay fees and stake.
ens: Ethereum Name Service (ENS) is a domain name system on Ethereum that replaces long wallet addresses with readable names like name.eth. The service launched in 2017 under Nick Johnson; ENS is the governance token of its DAO.
epol: iShares MSCI Poland (EPOL) invests in Poland's largest listed companies: banks, energy firms and retailers.
esp: Espresso (ESP) is a transaction-confirmation network for layer-2 blockchains based on BFT consensus. It gives rollups a near-instant, reliable view of each other's state, making interaction between chains easier and protecting against block reorgs.
etc: Ethereum Classic is the original Ethereum chain that kept running after the 2016 hard fork, when most of the community reversed the effects of The DAO hack. ETC sticks to the "code is law" principle and, unlike Ethereum, still uses Proof of Work mining.
eth: Ether (ETH) is the coin of Ethereum, the biggest smart-contract platform, which hosts DeFi, NFTs and stablecoins. Ether pays the network's transaction fees; Ethereum was co-founded by Vitalik Buterin in 2015.
etha: iShares Ethereum Trust (ETHA) is BlackRock's spot ether ETF, launched in 2024, giving brokerage-account access to ETH, the coin of the Ethereum network.
ethfi: Ether.fi is a liquid restaking protocol on Ethereum that is also growing into a crypto neobank with a card for spending and saving. Users stake ETH and keep it liquid through the eETH token; ETHFI is the governance token.
etn-token: Electroneum is an EVM-compatible layer-1 blockchain with transactions in a few seconds and instant finality. Founded in the UK by Richard Ells, the project targets mobile users and payments in developing countries; ETN is its native coin.
eurc: EURC is a euro-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle, the company behind USDC. Each token is backed one-to-one by euro reserves, it is issued under the EU's MiCA rules, and it runs on Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Base and other blockchains.
ev: Everything (EV) is a project that combines several DeFi protocols into one interconnected ecosystem. The EV token is used for governance, for using the services and for capturing value across all of the project's products.
evaa: EVAA Protocol is a decentralized lending protocol on the TON network. Users can supply crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral, including directly from Telegram; EVAA is the protocol's governance token.
ewg: iShares MSCI Germany (EWG) invests in large German companies such as SAP, Siemens, Allianz and Deutsche Telekom.
fartcoin: Fartcoin (FARTCOIN) is a meme coin on Solana that appeared in late 2024 out of jokes around the AI agent Truth Terminal. The token has no practical use and exists as an internet joke, so its price depends on community interest.
fast-retailing: Fast Retailing is a Japanese company from Yamaguchi that owns Uniqlo, Asia's largest clothing chain. It also runs the GU, Theory and Comptoir des Cotonniers brands; founder Tadashi Yanai turned a family shop into a global retailer of basic clothing.
fbtc: Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) is Fidelity's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024, which holds real bitcoin in Fidelity's own custody.
fdusd: First Digital USD (FDUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued since 2023 by First Digital Labs, part of Hong Kong-based First Digital Group. Each token is backed one-to-one by cash and short-term US Treasuries held in custody, and it is used mostly as a trading pair on major exchanges.
fet: The Artificial Superintelligence Alliance (ASI) was formed in 2024 by merging the AI projects Fetch.ai, SingularityNET and Ocean Protocol. It builds decentralized infrastructure for artificial intelligence and autonomous agents; FET is the alliance's shared token.
ff: FF is the token of Falcon Finance, a "universal collateral" protocol: users deposit crypto or tokenized real-world assets and mint the synthetic dollar USDf against them. This gives liquidity without selling the assets; FF is used for governance and staking.
fil: Filecoin is a decentralized data storage network where anyone can rent out spare disk space and get paid in FIL. It was created by Juan Benet's company Protocol Labs, also known for the IPFS protocol, and its mainnet launched in 2020.
flip: Chainflip (FLIP) is a decentralized protocol for swapping native crypto assets between different blockchains, for example bitcoin for ETH, without wrapped tokens or bridges. Validators stake FLIP, and part of the fees is used to burn the token.
floki: FLOKI is a memecoin launched in 2021 and named after Floki, Elon Musk's Shiba Inu dog. It has grown into a multi-chain token with its own ecosystem, including the Valhalla game, DeFi services and educational products.
flow: Flow (FLOW) is a layer-1 blockchain for consumer apps, created by Canadian studio Dapper Labs, the makers of CryptoKitties. NBA Top Shot and other digital collectibles run on it; FLOW is used for fees and staking.
flr: Flare is an Ethereum-compatible blockchain specialized in data: built-in oracles deliver prices and information from other networks and the internet. Its FAssets technology lets tokens without smart contracts, such as XRP, be used in DeFi.
fluid: Fluid is a DeFi protocol from the Instadapp team on Ethereum that combines lending and a decentralized exchange on shared liquidity, so collateral can work harder. The FLUID token replaced the former INST token and is used for governance.
flux: Flux is a decentralized cloud infrastructure where thousands of independent nodes provide computing power to run apps and websites. FLUX is mined and used to pay for services and to collateralize nodes.
folks: Folks Finance (FOLKS) is a cross-chain DeFi lending protocol: users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral across different blockchains from a single interface. The project grew up in the Algorand ecosystem, and FOLKS is its governance token.
form: Four (FORM), formerly BinaryX, is the token of the ecosystem linked to Four.meme, a popular memecoin launchpad on BNB Chain. FORM is used for staking, rewards and taking part in ecosystem projects.
fun: FUNToken (FUN) is a token for online gaming and the iGaming industry, launched in 2017. It is used for bets, payments and rewards on gaming platforms, with transparent settlement on the blockchain.
fxnw: FastX Network (FXNW) is a decentralized artificial-intelligence infrastructure for Web3 applications. The project aims to connect AI services with blockchain apps, and the FXNW token is used for payments and participation in the network.
gal: GAL is the former token of Galxe, a Web3 rewards and digital-credentials platform where projects run campaigns to attract users. GAL has migrated to G, the token of Galxe's Gravity network, so old coins are exchanged for new ones.
gala: GALA is the token of Gala Games, a US blockchain gaming platform founded in 2019 by Eric Schiermeyer. It is used to buy in-game items and NFTs, reward network node operators and vote; Gala also runs music and film branches.
gas: Gas (GAS) is the second token of the NEO network, used to pay fees for transactions and running smart contracts. NEO holders automatically receive GAS as a reward, so the two coins work as a pair: NEO for governance, GAS as fuel.
gasoline: RBOB gasoline is the US futures contract for petrol. Its price depends on crude oil, the summer driving season and how busy refineries are.
ge: GE Aerospace is a US jet engine maker based in Cincinnati, the successor of the General Electric conglomerate founded in 1892 with Thomas Edison's involvement. After the 2024 split it focuses on engines for passenger and military aircraft and their servicing.
genius: Genius (GENIUS) is the token of Genius Terminal, an on-chain terminal for professional crypto trading with a focus on privacy. It combines swaps, cross-chain transfers and wallet management in one interface to make DeFi easier to use.
geod: GEODNET is a decentralized network of ground stations that receive navigation satellite signals (GPS and other GNSS) and provide corrections for centimeter-level positioning. Drones, farm machinery and robots use this data; station owners earn GEOD for running them.
gev: GE Vernova is an American energy company based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, spun off from General Electric in 2024. It makes gas turbines, wind turbines, equipment for nuclear and hydro power, and technology for electricity grids.
ggbr: Goldfish Gold (GGBR) is a gold-backed token: each one represents 1/1000 of a troy ounce. The metal is held in a Wyoming trust as gold still in the ground at a deposit, not in bars, so the token gives on-chain access to that asset.
giggle: Giggle Fund (GIGGLE) is a BNB Chain meme token linked to Giggle Academy, an education initiative backed by Binance founder Changpeng Zhao. Part of the token's trading fees goes to donations for free education.
gild: Gilead Sciences is an American biopharmaceutical company based in California, founded in 1987. It is known for its HIV drugs (Biktarvy), hepatitis C treatments (Sovaldi, Harvoni) and the COVID-19 drug Veklury, and is expanding in cancer and inflammatory diseases.
gld: SPDR Gold Shares (GLD) is the biggest fund backed by physical gold: every share is backed by gold bars held in vaults.
glm: Golem (GLM) is one of the first decentralized computing projects, founded in Poland in 2016. Its network lets people rent out or rent computing power, for example for rendering and AI tasks; GLM is the payment token on Ethereum.
gmx: GMX is a decentralized exchange for perpetual futures and leveraged spot trading on Arbitrum and Avalanche. Traders trade straight from their wallets, liquidity providers earn a share of fees, and GMX is the governance and fee-sharing token.
gno: Gnosis is an ecosystem that began in 2015 as a prediction-market platform. It gave rise to the popular Safe multisig wallet, and today it develops the Gnosis Chain blockchain and payment services such as the Gnosis Pay card. GNO is used for staking and governance.
gohome: GOHOME is a meme token born from a January 2025 incident on the White House website, when the words Go Home appeared on its page. The community turned the episode into a meme, and the token trades purely as a meme asset with no product behind it.
gold: Gold is the classic safe-haven asset that has served as a store of value for thousands of years. Central banks, jewellers and investors buy it, especially in times of crisis, inflation or war.
gomining: GoMining is a digital Bitcoin mining platform backed by real data centers: users buy virtual miners as NFTs and receive daily rewards in BTC. The GOMINING token is used to pay maintenance fees, get discounts and for staking.
goog: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, based in Mountain View, California. It earns mainly from search and YouTube advertising, plus Google Cloud, Android and subscriptions, and develops the Gemini AI and Waymo robotaxis. Class C shares (GOOG) carry no voting rights.
googl: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, based in Mountain View, California; Google was founded in 1998 by Larry Page and Sergey Brin. It owns Google Search, YouTube, Android, Chrome, Google Cloud and the Gemini AI. Class A shares (GOOGL) carry voting rights.
gps: GoPlus Security (GPS) is a Web3 security network that checks tokens, smart contracts and addresses for scams and malicious activity. Its API is built into many wallets and exchanges; the GPS token is used to pay for security services.
gram: Gram (formerly Toncoin) is the native coin of the TON blockchain (The Open Network), originally conceived by Telegram's founders, the Durov brothers. The network is deeply integrated into Telegram, where the coin is used for transfers, fees, the built-in wallet and mini apps.
grass: Grass is a network where users share their unused internet bandwidth for rewards through a browser extension or app. This capacity helps collect public web data for training AI; the GRASS token runs on Solana.
grt: The Graph is an indexing protocol for blockchain data, often called the "Google of blockchains": it organizes data from Ethereum and other networks so apps can query it quickly through open APIs called subgraphs. GRT pays for queries and is staked by indexers who run the network.
gs: Goldman Sachs is one of the world's best-known investment banks, founded in 1869 in New York. It advises on large mergers and acquisitions, arranges share offerings, trades securities and manages money for wealthy clients and institutions.
gt: GateToken (GT) is the native token of the Gate (Gate.io) crypto exchange, founded in 2013. It gives discounts on trading fees and access to new token launches, and it pays fees on the exchange's own blockchain network.
gwei: ETHGas (GWEI) is an Ethereum blockspace infrastructure protocol that splits space in blocks into tradable units. It lets users buy block space in advance and get fast transaction confirmations.
h: Humanity Protocol (H) is a blockchain that verifies that each user is a unique human through Proof of Humanity, including palm scans. Its goal is to protect Web3 services from bots and fake accounts, and the H token is used in the network.
hbar: Hedera is a public network built on hashgraph technology, invented by Leemon Baird, for fast payments, tokenisation and enterprise apps. It is governed by a council of large companies including Google and IBM; HBAR pays fees and secures the network through staking.
hd: Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retail chain, founded in 1978 and based in Atlanta. It sells building materials, tools, garden equipment and household goods in the US, Canada and Mexico, serving both homeowners and professional builders.
heatoil: Heating oil is a refined oil product used for home heating and closely related to diesel fuel. Its price follows crude oil and winter demand.
hitachi: Hitachi is a Japanese industrial and technology conglomerate based in Tokyo, founded in 1910. It develops digital IT solutions (Lumada), power equipment and electricity grids, railway systems and industrial automation.
hnt: Helium (HNT) is a decentralized wireless network where people install hotspots and earn tokens for providing coverage. It first served IoT devices and now develops the Helium Mobile cellular service; since 2023 it has run on the Solana blockchain.
hogs: Lean hogs is a futures contract on the price of pork carcasses in the United States. It is driven by feed costs, exports to Asia and animal diseases.
holo: Holoworld (HOLO) is a platform for creating AI-agent virtual characters without coding: they can chat, livestream and interact with people across social networks. The project is developed by the studio Hologram Labs, and HOLO is the ecosystem token.
hot: Holo (HOT) is the token of Holo, a project building hosting for apps on Holochain, a platform for distributed applications that does not use a classic blockchain. Computer owners can rent out space and processing power for hosting and earn rewards.
hsbc-holdings: HSBC is a British-Asian banking group headquartered in London, founded in 1865 in Hong Kong as the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation. One of the world's largest banks, it earns most of its profit in Asia, especially Hong Kong.
hsk: HashKey Platform Token (HSK) is the ecosystem token of HashKey, a Hong Kong financial group that runs a licensed crypto exchange. It is used on the HashKey Chain network and to reward participants in the ecosystem.
htx: HTX is the governance token of HTX DAO, the ecosystem around the HTX crypto exchange (formerly Huobi), which is linked to Justin Sun. Token holders vote on the project's development and get perks in the exchange's services.
hype: Hyperliquid is its own layer-1 blockchain, best known for the decentralised exchange of the same name for perpetual futures and spot trading. HYPE is used for staking, fees and governance; the project is led by Jeff Yan.
ibe: Iberdrola is a Spanish energy company from Bilbao and one of the world's largest producers of wind and solar power. It owns power grids in Spain, the United Kingdom (ScottishPower), the United States (Avangrid) and Brazil (Neoenergia) and supplies electricity to millions of customers.
ibit: iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) is BlackRock's spot bitcoin ETF, launched in 2024. It lets investors own bitcoin through a regular brokerage account without a crypto wallet.
ibm: IBM is an American technology company based in Armonk, New York, founded in 1911. Once a leader in mainframes and personal computers, it now sells Red Hat hybrid cloud, enterprise software, the watsonx AI platform and consulting, and develops quantum computers.
icbc: ICBC (Industrial and Commercial Bank of China) is a state-owned Chinese bank based in Beijing and one of the largest banks in the world by assets. Founded in 1984, it serves hundreds of millions of customers and large companies; its H shares trade in Hong Kong.
icbc-cn: ICBC (A shares) are shares of Industrial and Commercial Bank of China traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. The state-owned Beijing bank, founded in 1984, is one of the world's largest and serves individuals, companies and the government through thousands of branches.
icln: iShares Global Clean Energy (ICLN) invests worldwide in solar, wind and other clean-energy companies.
icnt: Impossible Cloud Network (ICNT) is a decentralized protocol for business cloud services: storage, compute and networking. Hardware owners contribute resources and service providers use them; ICNT is needed for node collateral, access to resources and staking.
icp: Internet Computer is a blockchain from the Swiss DFINITY Foundation (Zurich), founded by Dominic Williams, launched in 2021. The network lets websites, services and AI agents run entirely on-chain without ordinary cloud servers; ICP pays for computation.
id: SPACE ID (ID) is a universal domain name service for Web3: users register and trade domains such as .bnb or .arb that replace long wallet addresses. The project was backed by Binance Labs, and ID is its governance token.
idol: MEET48 (IDOL) is a Web3 entertainment platform about virtual and real idols that combines AI, live streaming and game mechanics. Fans support their favorite performers and take part in shows, and the IDOL token serves as the ecosystem's currency.
imx: Immutable (IMX) is a blockchain gaming platform from Sydney, Australia, that runs the Ethereum layer-2 networks Immutable X and Immutable zkEVM. They let players trade in-game NFTs without paying gas fees; IMX is used for fees, staking and governance.
init: Initia is a blockchain network that joins many optimistic rollups into one interconnected system. Developers launch their own app-specific chains that can easily talk to each other; INIT is used for staking and governance.
inj: Injective is a layer-1 blockchain built with the Cosmos SDK for financial apps such as exchanges, derivatives and tokenized assets. It gives developers ready-made trading modules; INJ is used for staking, governance and paying network fees.
intc: Intel is a US chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 1968 by Robert Noyce and Gordon Moore. It is known for Core and Xeon processors for PCs and servers and is building a contract chip-manufacturing business, Intel Foundry.
io: io.net (IO) is a decentralized GPU network on Solana that pools graphics cards from data centers, mining farms and private computers into clusters for machine learning. AI engineers rent computing power for less than in regular clouds; IO is used for payments and rewards.
iost: IOST is a high-throughput blockchain platform launched in 2019 by a team backed by Sequoia and Matrix. It uses its own Proof of Believability consensus and focuses on fast, cheap decentralized apps.
iota: IOTA is an open-source blockchain project run by the Berlin-based IOTA Foundation and founded in 2015. Originally built for the Internet of Things, it now focuses on digital identity, trade data and tokenization; the IOTA token pays fees and is used for staking.
iotx: IoTeX is a blockchain platform launched in 2017 that connects real-world devices to blockchain and AI. It feeds verified data from sensors, cars and gadgets into decentralized apps and develops the DePIN sector; IOTX is the network's native coin.
irys: Irys (IRYS) is a layer-1 blockchain that combines data storage with smart-contract execution, formerly known as Bundlr. It is designed for large volumes of data for AI and Web3 applications.
isrg: Intuitive Surgical is a California company founded in 1995 and a pioneer of robotic surgery. Its da Vinci system lets surgeons perform minimally invasive operations with robotic arms; the company earns money from instruments and service.
ita: iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense (ITA) invests in American defence contractors and aerospace companies that build aircraft, missiles and space systems.
itx: Inditex is a Spanish fashion giant from Galicia founded by Amancio Ortega, owner of the chains Zara, Pull&Bear, Massimo Dutti, Bershka, Stradivarius and Oysho. It is known for fast fashion: new collections reach thousands of stores worldwide within weeks.
ivv: iShares Core S&P 500 (IVV) is BlackRock's low-cost ETF on the S&P 500 index and one of the largest ETFs in the world.
iwm: iShares Russell 2000 (IWM) tracks the Russell 2000 index of small US companies. It is more sensitive to the economy and interest rates than the S&P 500.
jasmy: JasmyCoin is the token of Jasmy, a Tokyo-based Japanese company founded by former Sony executives. Jasmy builds an Internet of Things platform where users keep control of their own personal data; JASMY is an ERC-20 token on Ethereum.
jellyjelly: Jelly-My-Jelly (JELLYJELLY) is a meme token on Solana linked to the video app JellyJelly, created by Venmo co-founder Iqram Magdon-Ismail. The token became a symbol of the app's community and trades as a meme asset.
jepi: JPMorgan Equity Premium Income (JEPI) holds S&P 500 stocks and sells options on them to pay a high monthly income, giving up part of the upside in return.
jepq: JPMorgan Nasdaq Equity Premium Income (JEPQ) holds Nasdaq-100 stocks and sells options to fund monthly payouts, trading some growth for income.
jnj: Johnson & Johnson is a US healthcare company based in New Brunswick, New Jersey, founded in 1886. It develops prescription drugs for oncology, immunology and neuroscience, plus medical devices for surgery and cardiology; its consumer brands were spun off as Kenvue in 2023.
jpm: JPMorgan Chase is the largest US bank, headquartered in New York, with roots going back to 1799. It serves millions of customers under the Chase brand and runs investment banking, asset management and payments for big companies; it is led by Jamie Dimon.
jst: JUST (JST) is the governance token of the JUST decentralized finance ecosystem on the TRON blockchain, linked to Justin Sun. The platform includes the JustLend lending service and stablecoin tools, and JST holders vote on protocol settings.
jto: JTO is the governance token of Jito Network, a key piece of Solana infrastructure. Jito offers liquid staking of SOL through the JitoSOL token and a modified validator client that lets validators and stakers earn extra income from MEV.
jup: Jupiter is the largest token-swap aggregator on Solana: it searches across decentralized exchanges for the best rate. It also offers perpetual futures, limit orders and new token launches; JUP is the governance token.
kaia: Kaia is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain formed in 2024 by merging the Klaytn (from Kakao) and Finschia (from LINE) networks. It aims to bring Web3 to millions of users in Asia directly inside the KakaoTalk and LINE messengers; KAIA is its native coin.
kaito: KAITO is the token of Kaito, a platform that uses AI to collect and analyze crypto news, social media and discussions. Its InfoFi network rewards content creators and researchers for the attention they attract; KAITO is used for rewards, staking and governance.
kas: Kaspa is a Proof of Work cryptocurrency launched in November 2021 with no premine or presale. It uses a BlockDAG structure (the GHOSTDAG protocol), which lets blocks be created in parallel and confirms transfers very quickly.
kava: Kava (KAVA) is a layer-1 blockchain that connects the Ethereum and Cosmos ecosystems and offers DeFi services that work like a decentralized bank, such as lending and stablecoins. KAVA is used for staking, fees and governance.
kcs: KuCoin Token (KCS) is the native token of KuCoin, an international crypto exchange founded in 2017. Holders get discounts on trading fees and a share of bonuses, and KCS also pays fees on the KCC network.
kgen: KGeN is a Web3 gaming platform that builds a network of verified real players and lets game publishers reach a live audience instead of bots. The project has a strong presence in India; KGEN is the ecosystem token.
kii: KiiChain (KII) is a layer-1 blockchain built for emerging markets, especially Latin America. It focuses on stablecoin payments, currency exchange and tokenizing real-world assets for local businesses.
kite: Kite is a blockchain for the "agentic economy", where AI agents can make payments on their own and securely. The network supports the x402 standard that lets machines pay for online services; KITE is its native token for staking and fees.
klac: KLA Corporation is an American maker of process-control equipment for semiconductor manufacturing, based in California. Its inspection and metrology systems find defects on silicon wafers and photomasks; its customers are the world's largest chipmakers.
kmno: Kamino is a DeFi platform on Solana that combines lending, borrowing, leverage and automated liquidity management. It began as the easiest way to earn from providing liquidity through one-click, auto-compounding strategies; KMNO is the governance token.
kntq: Kinetiq (KNTQ) is the token of a liquid staking protocol on Hyperliquid that issues kHYPE for staked HYPE. The team also builds Markets.xyz for round-the-clock futures trading on stocks, currencies and commodities.
ko: The Coca-Cola Company is an American company from Atlanta and the world's largest maker of soft drinks; the Coca-Cola drink itself was invented in 1886. It also owns Sprite, Fanta, Dasani water and Costa Coffee, and sells its products in more than 200 countries.
ksm: Kusama (KSM) is a blockchain built on the same code as Polkadot, created by Gavin Wood as a «canary network» for testing new features. Projects test upgrades here in real conditions before launching on Polkadot; KSM is used for staking and governance.
kta: Keeta (KTA) is a high-performance layer-1 blockchain designed to connect transfers across different blockchains and traditional payment systems. The project is backed by former Google CEO Eric Schmidt, and KTA is used to pay network fees.
kub: KUB Coin (KUB) is the native coin of KUB Chain (formerly Bitkub Chain), the blockchain created by Thailand's crypto exchange Bitkub. It is used to pay network fees, for staking and in ecosystem apps in Thailand.
kweb: KraneShares CSI China Internet (KWEB) invests in Chinese internet companies such as Alibaba, Tencent, PDD and Meituan.
kweichow-moutai: Kweichow Moutai is a Chinese state-owned maker of baijiu, a strong grain liquor, from the town of Maotai in Guizhou province. Its Moutai liquor is China's most prestigious alcoholic drink, given as a gift on holidays and served at official banquets.
lcx: LCX is a crypto exchange and blockchain company from Vaduz, Liechtenstein, registered under the country's blockchain law. It offers trading, storage and tokenization of digital assets for regulated markets in Europe, and the LCX token gives users fee discounts and access to platform services.
ldo: Lido DAO is the governance token of Lido, the largest liquid staking protocol on Ethereum, launched in 2020. Users stake ETH and receive the stETH token in return, which they can freely use in DeFi; LDO holders vote on the protocol's parameters.
leo: LEO Token is the utility token of iFinex, the owner of the Bitfinex exchange, issued in 2019. Holders get trading-fee discounts on Bitfinex, and the company regularly buys back and burns tokens.
lin: Linde is the world's largest industrial gases company, formed in 2018 by the merger of Germany's Linde AG and America's Praxair. It supplies oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen and helium to hospitals, steel, chemical and electronics makers and also builds gas plants.
linea: Linea (LINEA) is an Ethereum layer-2 network built on zkEVM technology by Consensys, the company behind the MetaMask wallet. It makes transactions cheaper and faster while staying fully Ethereum-compatible, and burns part of the ETH collected in network fees.
link: Chainlink is a decentralised oracle network that feeds smart contracts with real-world data such as prices, exchange rates and event results. Launched in 2017 under Sergey Nazarov, it uses LINK to pay node operators.
lion: Loaded Lions (LION) is the token of the flagship NFT collection of the Crypto.com exchange, featuring lion avatars. It is used within the collection's ecosystem on the Cronos network for rewards, access to events and the holders' community.
lista: Lista DAO (LISTA) is a liquid staking and lending protocol on BNB Chain. Users stake BNB and receive slisBNB, and can borrow the lisUSD stablecoin against various assets as collateral; LISTA is the governance token.
lit: LIT is the token of Lighter, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange built as a ZK rollup on Ethereum. Its standout feature is order matching and liquidations that are verifiable with cryptographic proofs, at speeds close to centralized exchanges.
lly: Eli Lilly is an American pharmaceutical company from Indianapolis, founded in 1876. It is known for insulin, the diabetes and obesity drugs Mounjaro and Zepbound, and medicines in oncology and immunology, and is one of the world's largest drugmakers.
lobo: LOBO•THE•WOLF•PUP (LOBO) is a meme token on Bitcoin's Runes protocol with a wolf-pup mascot. It became one of the first popular runes, and part of the fees paid at launch went to Bitcoin miners.
lpt: Livepeer (LPT) is a decentralized network for processing and transcoding video, launched in 2017. Node operators provide GPU power to re-encode streams and, more recently, to generate AI video; LPT is staked to distribute work and earn rewards.
lrcx: Lam Research is a US maker of chip-manufacturing equipment based in Fremont, California, founded in 1980. Its tools etch and deposit thin layers of material on silicon wafers; customers include the largest memory and processor makers.
lsk: Lisk (LSK) is a project founded in Berlin in 2016 that now operates as a layer-2 network on Ethereum. It builds financial infrastructure for businesses to store, transfer and invest money in fiat currencies and stablecoins.
ltc: Litecoin is one of the oldest cryptocurrencies, created in 2011 by former Google engineer Charlie Lee from bitcoin's code. Blocks arrive four times faster than bitcoin's, which is why it is often called 'silver to bitcoin's gold'.
luna: Terra (LUNA) is the native token of the new Terra blockchain, created in 2022 after the collapse of the algorithmic stablecoin UST. The old network was renamed Terra Classic (LUNC), while the new one runs on the Cosmos SDK and uses LUNA for staking and governance.
lunc: Terra Luna Classic is the original Terra blockchain left after the collapse of the UST stablecoin in May 2022. The community then launched a new Terra 2.0 network, while the old chain and its LUNC coin live on under community governance that burns tokens.
m: MemeCore is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for meme coins. The project aims to turn memes from pure speculation into a tool for culture and communities: anyone can launch tokens and earn rewards for helping them grow popular.
ma: Mastercard is a US payments company headquartered in Purchase, New York, and one of the world's two biggest card networks alongside Visa. It runs the network behind Mastercard, Maestro and Cirrus cards, connecting banks, merchants and cardholders; it does not issue cards or lend money itself.
