magic: Treasure (MAGIC) is a decentralized gaming ecosystem that grew up on the Arbitrum network. Treasure builds games and AI-powered entertainment products, and MAGIC is its native token for payments and rewards.
magma: Magma Finance is a decentralized exchange on the Sui blockchain. It uses concentrated and adaptive liquidity so traders get better prices and liquidity providers earn more fees; the MAGMA token is used for governance and rewards.
mana: Decentraland (MANA) is a virtual world on Ethereum, opened to the public in 2020, where users buy plots of LAND as NFTs, build scenes, host events and sell digital items. MANA is the in-world currency and the voting token of its DAO.
marscoin: MARSCOIN is a token on BNB Chain conceived as a crypto asset paired with a company's stock. It is a speculative meme project with no standalone product, so its price depends on community interest.
mask: Mask Network (MASK) is a project that connects ordinary social networks with Web3: its browser extension lets people encrypt messages and send cryptocurrency and NFTs directly inside Twitter (X). MASK serves as the governance token.
mbg-token: MBG is the token of MultiBank Group, one of the large forex and derivatives brokers, founded in 2005. The token is used within the group's ecosystem for trading discounts, staking and access to tokenized assets.
mc: LVMH is the world's largest luxury goods group, based in Paris and formed in 1987 by the merger of Moët Hennessy and Louis Vuitton. It controls more than 70 houses, including Louis Vuitton, Dior, Tiffany, Bulgari, Sephora, Moët & Chandon champagne and Hennessy cognac; it is led by Bernard Arnault.
mcd: McDonald's is the world's largest fast-food restaurant chain, headquartered in Chicago, built up from 1955 by Ray Kroc. Most of its restaurants are run by franchisees, and the company earns mainly from rent and royalties paid by them.
me: Magic Eden is one of the largest NFT marketplaces, founded in 2021 in the Solana ecosystem. It lets people buy and sell NFTs, Ordinals and Runes on Bitcoin, Solana, Ethereum, Base and other networks; the ME token is used for governance and rewards.
mediatek: MediaTek is a Taiwanese chip designer based in Hsinchu, founded in 1997. It designs Dimensity and Helio processors for Android smartphones as well as chips for TVs, Wi-Fi routers, tablets and smart devices; it has no factories of its own.
mega: MegaETH (MEGA) is an Ethereum layer-2 network marketed as a «real-time blockchain» with millisecond latency and very high throughput. It stays Ethereum-compatible, so apps can run almost instantly without changing their tools.
melania: Melania Meme (MELANIA) is a memecoin on the Solana network launched in January 2025 in Melania Trump's name. The token is presented as a digital collectible and a sign of support, with no practical function or ownership rights.
merl: Merlin Chain (MERL) is a bitcoin layer-2 network based on ZK-rollup technology, launched in 2024. It lets users move BTC, Runes and BRC-20 tokens into an environment with cheap transactions and DeFi apps; MERL is the network's governance token.
met-token: Meteora is a liquidity platform on Solana with dynamic pools and a DLMM mechanism, where trading fees change with market volatility. Many new Solana tokens and memecoins launch and trade through Meteora; MET is the project's governance token.
meta: Meta Platforms is a US company from Menlo Park, California, founded by Mark Zuckerberg in 2004 as Facebook. It owns Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp and Messenger, earns mostly from advertising, and develops Llama AI, smart glasses and Quest VR headsets.
metal: Metal Blockchain (METAL) is a layer-0 blockchain from Metallicus built on Avalanche's consensus technology. It targets payments and financial services for banks and is linked to the Metal Pay digital banking app; METAL is used for fees and staking.
mew: cat in a dogs world (MEW) is a Solana meme token whose idea is a "cat in a world of dogs" – a challenge to the many dog-themed meme coins. It runs purely on its community's meme culture.
mina: Mina Protocol (MINA) is a blockchain whose size stays at about 22 kilobytes thanks to recursive zero-knowledge proofs. That lets anyone verify the network even from a smartphone; MINA is used for fees and staking.
mitsubishi-ufj: Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) is Japan's largest banking group, headquartered in Tokyo. It provides retail, corporate and investment banking, asset management and brokerage services, and owns a large stake in the US bank Morgan Stanley.
mmt: Momentum is a decentralized exchange with concentrated liquidity on the Sui network. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity, while MMT is used for governance and rewards for protocol participants.
mnt: Mantle is a layer-2 network for Ethereum that grew out of BitDAO and is closely linked to the Bybit crypto exchange. It lowers transaction costs for DeFi apps; MNT pays fees and is used for voting in the ecosystem.
moca: Moca Network (MOCA) is digital identity infrastructure from Animoca Brands: one universal account for a person's assets, identity and reputation across different blockchains. The project grew out of the Mocaverse NFT collection, and MOCA is used across its ecosystem.
mog: Mog Coin (MOG) is a meme token on Ethereum launched in 2023, inspired by the internet slang word mog, meaning to outshine someone. It runs on the community's viral meme culture and has no separate product.
mon: Monad is a high-performance Layer 1 blockchain that is fully compatible with Ethereum (EVM) and executes transactions in parallel for speed and low fees. Its mainnet launched in November 2025; MON pays network fees and is used for staking.
moodeng: Moo Deng (MOODENG) is a Solana meme token dedicated to Moo Deng, the pygmy hippo from Thailand's Khao Kheow Open Zoo who became an internet star in 2024. The token has no product of its own.
morpho: Morpho is a decentralized lending protocol on Ethereum, Base and other networks where users deposit assets to earn interest or borrow against collateral. It lets anyone create separate isolated markets and vaults; MORPHO is the governance token.
move: Movement is a blockchain network that brings the Move programming language to developers, including in the Ethereum ecosystem. Move was created at Meta for the Diem project and focuses on smart-contract safety; MOVE is the network's token.
mplx: Metaplex (MPLX) is the leading tokenization platform on Solana: its standards and tools are used to create most NFTs and many tokens on that network. MPLX is the protocol's governance token.
mrk: Merck & Co. (known as MSD outside the US and Canada) is an American pharmaceutical company from New Jersey with roots going back to 1891. It makes the cancer drug Keytruda, the HPV vaccine Gardasil and medicines for animals.
mrvl: Marvell Technology is an American designer of semiconductors for data infrastructure, founded in 1995. It makes chips for data centres, networking, storage and cars, including custom AI processors built for the big cloud companies.
ms: Morgan Stanley is a US investment bank headquartered in New York, founded in 1935. It manages wealth for affluent clients, trades securities and advises on mergers and acquisitions; it also owns the E*Trade brokerage platform.
msft: Microsoft is a US technology company based in Redmond, Washington, founded in 1975 by Bill Gates and Paul Allen. It develops Windows, Office, the Azure cloud, LinkedIn, Xbox and the Copilot assistant, and is a key partner of OpenAI.
mu: Micron Technology is a US memory maker from Boise, Idaho, founded in 1978. It produces DRAM, NAND flash, SSDs and high-bandwidth HBM memory for AI accelerators, and also sells products under the Crucial brand.
mubarak: Mubarak is a BNB Chain meme token with an Arabic name meaning "blessed". It became popular in 2025 after Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) mentioned it and bought some.
mvl: MVL is a blockchain ecosystem for mobility that collects data about a car over its whole life from dealers, repair shops and rental companies. The Singapore-based project also launched the TADA ride-hailing service in Southeast Asia; MVL is the token for rewards and payments.
mx: MX is the native token of the crypto exchange MEXC (formerly MXC), founded in 2018. MX holders get trading fee discounts, access to new token distributions and a vote on which coins get listed on the exchange.
natgas: Natural gas (US Henry Hub) is a fuel for heating and power plants and a raw material for the chemical industry. Its price is highly seasonal and depends on the weather and LNG exports.
near: NEAR Protocol is a layer-1 blockchain for smart contracts and apps that is increasingly focused on AI agents. Its co-founder, Ukrainian-born Illia Polosukhin, is one of the authors of the famous Transformer paper behind modern AI.
nee: NextEra Energy is one of the largest US energy companies, headquartered in Florida. Its subsidiary Florida Power & Light supplies electricity to millions of customers, while NextEra Energy Resources is one of the world's biggest producers of wind and solar power.
neiro: Neiro is a meme coin named after Neiro, the Shiba Inu adopted in 2024 by the owner of Kabosu, the dog behind the Doge meme. The token runs on its community and the popularity of dog memes and has no technical function of its own.
neo: NEO is a Chinese smart-contract blockchain founded in 2014 as Antshares by Da Hongfei and Erik Zhang. It is often called the «Chinese Ethereum»; NEO holders receive the network's second token, GAS, which is used to pay fees.
nes: Nesa (NES) is a privacy-focused layer-1 blockchain for decentralized artificial intelligence. Its encrypted inference technology lets AI models run on confidential data without exposing it; NES pays for fees, model queries and running network nodes.
nesn: Nestlé is a Swiss company based in Vevey, the world's largest food maker, founded in 1866 by Henri Nestlé. It is known for the brands Nescafé, Nespresso, KitKat and Maggi, Purina pet food and baby food.
nex: Nexus (NEX) is a layer-1 blockchain project for verifiable finance, designed to run decentralized exchanges. It uses zero-knowledge (ZK) technology to prove computations, and the NEX token is meant to power the network.
nexo: Nexo is a crypto platform founded in 2018 that offers loans backed by crypto collateral, interest on deposits, exchange and a payment card. Holding the NEXO token gives users better rates, cheaper loans and cashback.
nflx: Netflix is the world's largest streaming service for films and series, based in Los Gatos, California, and founded in 1997 by Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph. It began by renting DVDs by mail and now produces its own hits such as Stranger Things and Squid Game.
nft: AINFT (formerly APENFT) is a project in the TRON ecosystem that combines NFTs with artificial intelligence. The NFT token serves as its governance token: holders take part in votes on how the platform develops.
night: Midnight is a privacy-focused blockchain built by Input Output, the developer of Cardano, as a partner chain. Zero-knowledge proofs let applications verify data without revealing it; NIGHT is the network's native token.
nil: Nillion (NIL) is a decentralized network for working with encrypted data, letting computations run on it without revealing the contents. It is used for private AI apps and protected markets, and the NIL token pays for the service and is staked.
nmr: Numeraire (NMR) is the token of Numerai, a San Francisco hedge fund founded in 2015 by Richard Craib. The fund runs a tournament where data scientists submit stock-market prediction models and stake NMR on their quality: accurate models are rewarded, poor ones lose their stake.
nock: Nockchain (NOCK) is a layer-1 blockchain where nodes «mine» zero-knowledge proofs (ZK Proof of Work) instead of ordinary hashes. The project is connected to the Urbit community and the Nock programming language.
not: Notcoin (NOT) is a token on the TON network that grew out of a viral 2024 tap-to-earn game in Telegram, where millions of users tapped a coin on screen. The project became one of the biggest gateways for newcomers into crypto through Telegram.
novn: Novartis is a Swiss pharmaceutical company based in Basel, formed in 1996 by the merger of Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz. It develops innovative medicines for cancer, heart disease and immunology, including Entresto, Kisqali and Cosentyx.
npc: Non-Playable Coin (NPC) is an Ethereum meme coin inspired by the "non-playable character" meme. Its supply equals Earth's population as of 26 July 2023, and each token can be turned into an NFT and back.
nvda: Nvidia is a US chipmaker based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang. Known for GeForce graphics cards, its main business today is GPUs and systems for data centres that train and run artificial intelligence.
nxpc: Nexpace (NXPC) is the token of MapleStory Universe, a blockchain ecosystem built by South Korean game giant Nexon around its cult game MapleStory. It is used to create and trade in-game NFT items and in the economy of the games in this universe.
oats: Oats are a grain used for cereal flakes, porridge and animal feed. The futures market is small, so prices can swing sharply on the weather in Canada and the US.
ocean: Ocean Protocol is a blockchain ecosystem for sharing data and related services, founded in Singapore in 2017. It lets people sell and buy access to datasets and AI computing without handing over the data itself; in 2024 it joined the ASI Alliance with Fetch.ai and SingularityNET.
ojuice: Frozen concentrated orange juice is a small futures market. Prices depend on orange harvests in Florida and Brazil, hurricanes and citrus diseases.
okb: OKB is the token of the OKX crypto exchange (formerly OKEx), launched in 2018. It gives discounts on trading fees and access to new token launches, and pays fees on X Layer, OKX's layer-2 network.
omi: ECOMI (OMI) is the token behind VeVe, a mobile platform for licensed digital collectibles in the form of NFTs. Collections from major brands such as Marvel, DC and Disney are released on VeVe; OMI is used in the loyalty program and for purchases.
ondo: Ondo is a real-world asset tokenization project that brings US Treasuries, funds and stocks onto the blockchain, making them accessible to crypto investors. The Ondo Foundation was set up in 2022, and ONDO is the ecosystem's governance token.
one: ONEchain (ONE), formerly CROSS, is a Layer 1 blockchain for games developed by South Korea's NEXUS. It lets studios turn in-game currencies and items into tokens and NFTs that go to the player's wallet; ONE is the network's native token.
ong: Ontology Gas (ONG) is the token used to pay transaction fees on the Ontology blockchain. It is gradually released to ONT holders and stakers, because the network uses a two-token model: ONT for staking and governance, ONG as the "gas".
ont: Ontology (ONT) is a public blockchain founded in 2017 by the Chinese team Onchain, focused on digital identity and trusted data. ONT is used for staking and governance and generates the network's second token, ONG, which pays transaction fees.
op: Optimism is a Layer 2 network for Ethereum built on optimistic rollup technology, making transactions cheaper and faster. Its open-source OP Stack powers the Superchain of connected networks, including Coinbase's Base; OP is the governance token.
open: OpenLedger (OPEN) is a blockchain for artificial intelligence where data, models, apps and agents can be monetized. It tracks how much each data provider contributes to a model's work and shares out rewards accordingly; OPEN is used for fees and incentives.
opg: OpenGradient (OPG) is a decentralized network for hosting, running and verifying AI models. Model outputs are proven cryptographically, so smart contracts and apps can trust AI results; the OPG token pays for the service and rewards participants.
or: L'Oréal is the world's largest cosmetics company, headquartered near Paris and founded in 1909 by chemist Eugène Schueller. It owns L'Oréal Paris, Garnier, Maybelline, Lancôme, Yves Saint Laurent Beauté, La Roche-Posay and CeraVe, selling skin, hair and makeup products.
orbs: Orbs (ORBS) is an Israeli blockchain project founded in 2017 that works as a supporting execution layer for other networks. DeFi tools such as dLIMIT and dTWAP for decentralized exchanges are built on it; ORBS is used for staking.
orca: Orca (ORCA) is one of the first decentralized exchanges on Solana, known for its simple interface. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity in concentrated-liquidity pools called Whirlpools to earn a share of fees; ORCA is the governance token.
orcl: Oracle is an American technology company founded in 1977 by Larry Ellison. It is known for the Oracle Database, enterprise software and its Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, which builds data centers for AI; Oracle also owns Java.
ordi: ORDI is the first token of the BRC-20 standard on the Bitcoin network, created in 2023 using the Ordinals protocol. It showed that tokens can be issued directly on Bitcoin's blockchain; it has no practical function and trades as a symbol of that trend.
ozo: Ozone Chain is a blockchain that presents itself as resistant to quantum-computer attacks thanks to built-in quantum cryptography technology. It lets developers build decentralized applications with low fees; OZO is the network's native coin.
palladium: Palladium is a rare platinum-group metal that goes almost entirely into catalytic converters for petrol engines. The main producers are Russia and South Africa.
panw: Palo Alto Networks is a US cybersecurity company based in Santa Clara, California, founded in 2005. It sells next-generation firewalls, cloud security and AI-powered platforms for detecting attacks, including Prisma and Cortex.
paxg: PAX Gold (PAXG) is a token issued by Paxos in which each coin is backed by one troy ounce of London Good Delivery gold held in professional vaults in London. Launched in 2019 and overseen by the New York regulator, it lets people own gold on Ethereum and redeem it for bars.
peaq: peaq (PEAQ) is a blockchain for the «machine economy» that gives robots, vehicles, devices, sensors and AI agents digital identities, wallets and the ability to pay each other. DePIN projects run on it, letting people earn from their devices' data and services.
pearl: Pearl is a layer-1 blockchain built on Proof of Useful Work: mining happens as a by-product of useful AI computation on graphics cards. The same GPUs train or run AI models while also securing the network; PEARL is its native coin.
pendle: Pendle is a DeFi protocol that splits yield-bearing assets into two parts — the principal and the future yield — which can be traded separately. This lets users lock in a fixed yield or speculate on how it changes; PENDLE is the governance and rewards token.
pengu: PENGU is the official token of Pudgy Penguins, one of the best-known NFT collections of cartoon penguins. The brand has grown beyond crypto, with Pudgy Penguins toys sold in major retail stores; the token launched on Solana in late 2024.
people: ConstitutionDAO (PEOPLE) is the token of an online community that in November 2021 raised over $40 million in crypto to bid at Sotheby's for an original copy of the US Constitution. The auction was lost, but the token remained a symbol of the movement.
pep: PepsiCo is an American food and beverage giant based in Purchase, New York. Besides Pepsi it owns Lay's, Doritos, Cheetos, Gatorade, Quaker and 7UP (outside the US); it was formed in 1965 by the merger of Pepsi-Cola and Frito-Lay.
pepe: Pepe is a meme coin on Ethereum dedicated to the famous Pepe the Frog internet meme, launched in 2023. The token has no hidden functions or transaction taxes and relies on the meme's popularity and community activity.
petrochina: PetroChina is China's largest oil and gas company, based in Beijing and created in 1999 as a subsidiary of state-owned CNPC. It produces oil and gas, refines them, owns trunk pipelines and runs a network of filling stations across the country.
pfe: Pfizer is one of the world's largest pharmaceutical companies, founded in 1849 in New York. It develops medicines and vaccines for cancer, infections and heart disease, and is known for the COVID-19 vaccine made with BioNTech and for drugs such as Viagra and Lipitor.
pg: Procter & Gamble is an American consumer goods maker based in Cincinnati, founded in 1837. It owns brands such as Gillette, Pampers, Tide, Ariel, Head & Shoulders, Oral-B and Fairy, and is known for decades of uninterrupted dividend increases.
pgr: Progressive is one of the largest car insurers in the US, headquartered in Mayfield Village, Ohio. It sells auto, motorcycle, home and business insurance online and through agents, and is known for its TV ads featuring the character Flo.
pha: Phala Network (PHA) is a decentralized cloud for confidential computing that uses secure processor enclaves (TEE). It lets AI agents work safely with blockchains; the PHA token is used for payments and staking.
pi: Pi Network is a social cryptocurrency launched in 2019 by Stanford graduates. Users "mine" Pi in a mobile app with a single tap and no energy cost, and the network's open mainnet went live in February 2025.
pieverse: Pieverse is compliance-focused payment infrastructure for Web3. The protocol records transactions on-chain as verifiable receipts and timestamps (including on the x402 standard), so businesses and AI agents can settle payments transparently; it runs on BNB Chain.
ping-an: Ping An Insurance (A shares) are shares of the Shenzhen-based Chinese financial group Ping An listed on the Shanghai exchange. Founded in 1988, the group works in life and property insurance, banking and asset management, and develops online healthcare services.
platinum: Platinum is a rare precious metal mined mostly in South Africa. Its main uses are catalytic converters for cars, jewellery and hydrogen technologies.
pltr: Palantir is an American data analytics company headquartered in Denver, founded in 2003 by Peter Thiel, Alex Karp and others. Its Gotham, Foundry and AIP platforms help governments, armed forces and corporations analyze large datasets and put artificial intelligence to work.
plume: Plume (PLUME) is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for tokenized real-world assets (RWA). It lets assets such as loans, bonds or commodities be issued on-chain and used in DeFi for lending and earning yield.
pm: Philip Morris International is a tobacco company based in Stamford, Connecticut, that sells Marlboro outside the United States. It is pushing smoke-free products: IQOS heated-tobacco devices and ZYN nicotine pouches.
pnut: Peanut the Squirrel (PNUT) is a meme token on Solana named after Peanut, a squirrel popular on Instagram that New York state authorities seized and euthanized in November 2024. The story went viral, and the token became a symbol of community protest.
pol: POL is the native token of the Polygon network, which replaced MATIC in 2024. Polygon is a family of Ethereum scaling solutions popular for payments and tokenization; POL pays network fees and is staked to secure Polygon chains.
polyx: Polymesh (POLYX) is a layer-1 blockchain for regulated assets such as tokenized stocks and bonds, built by the Polymath team. It has built-in identity checks and compliance rules; POLYX is used for fees and staking.
popcat: Popcat (POPCAT) is a Solana meme token inspired by the viral meme of a cat named Oatmeal that "pops" its mouth open in an O shape. It is driven purely by meme culture.
powr: Powerledger is an Australian tech company founded in Perth in 2016 that builds blockchain software for decentralized energy markets. Its platform tracks and trades electricity, including solar power between neighbours, and environmental certificates; POWR is the platform access token.
pro: Propy is an American blockchain platform for real-estate deals that automates buying a home, from signing the contract to recording the title. In 2017 it handled one of the first property sales recorded on a blockchain; the PRO token is used in its ecosystem.
prom: Prom (PROM) is a modular Layer 2 network built on zkEVM technology that connects different blockchains, both Ethereum-compatible and not. The project grew out of the Prometeus platform; PROM is used to pay fees and for staking.
pros: Pharos (PROS) is an Ethereum-compatible layer-1 blockchain built for payments and tokenized real-world assets. The network is designed for very high throughput, and PROS is its native token.
prove: Succinct (PROVE) is a decentralized network of provers that generates zero-knowledge proofs for blockchains and apps. The team built the SP1 zkVM, and the PROVE token is used to pay for proofs and for staking.
pump: PUMP is the token of Pump.fun, a Solana platform that since 2024 lets anyone launch their own meme coin in about a minute. Pump.fun became one of the main venues of the meme coin boom, and part of its revenue goes to buying back PUMP.
purr: Purr (PURR) is a cat-themed memecoin, the first spot token on the Hyperliquid network, launched without a sale. Half of the supply was distributed to Hyperliquid users; the token has no planned utility and exists as a community symbol.
pyth: Pyth Network is a decentralized oracle network that delivers real-time prices of stocks, crypto, currencies and commodities to blockchains. The data comes directly from exchanges and trading firms; PYTH is the network's governance token.
pyusd: PayPal USD (PYUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched by PayPal in August 2023 and issued by Paxos. It is backed by dollar deposits and short-term US Treasuries, runs on Ethereum and Solana, and can be bought, sent and used for payments inside PayPal and Venmo in the US.
q-token: Quack AI (Q) is a project building a governance layer for the AI agent economy, where agents, users and apps interact under verifiable rules. It supports sign-to-pay, gasless payments across blockchains based on the x402 standard; Q is the ecosystem token.
qcom: Qualcomm is a US chip designer from San Diego, founded in 1985. It makes Snapdragon processors and modems for smartphones, cars and PCs, and earns licensing fees on its patents for 3G, 4G and 5G wireless technology.
qnt: Quant is a London-based company founded by Gilbert Verdian whose Overledger technology connects different blockchains with each other and with banking systems. The QNT token is needed to access the platform and pay for licences for developers and businesses.
qqq: Invesco QQQ is an ETF that tracks the Nasdaq-100, the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq. Tech giants such as Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia and Amazon dominate it.
qqqm: Invesco Nasdaq 100 (QQQM) tracks the same Nasdaq-100 index as QQQ but with a lower annual fee, aimed at long-term investors.
qrl: Quantum Resistant Ledger (QRL) is a blockchain launched in 2018 and secured by XMSS signatures that resist attacks from future quantum computers. Its core idea is to keep funds safe even once quantum machines can break today's usual cryptography.
qtum: Qtum (QTUM) is a Singapore-based blockchain launched in 2017 that combines Bitcoin's UTXO transaction model with Ethereum-style smart contracts. It runs on proof of stake, so QTUM holders earn rewards for helping secure the network.
qubic: Qubic (QUBIC) is a layer-1 blockchain founded by Sergey Ivancheglo, a co-founder of IOTA. It offers fee-free transactions and «useful» mining, where miners' computing power goes toward training artificial intelligence.
rail: Railgun (RAIL) is a smart contract system for private transactions on Ethereum and other networks that uses zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). It lets users trade and lend on DeFi platforms while hiding their balances and wallet history; RAIL is the governance token.
rain: Rain is a decentralised protocol for options and prediction markets on the Arbitrum network. Anyone can create a market on an event and trade it; public markets are settled by an AI oracle, while in private ones the creator decides the result.
rave: RaveDAO (RAVE) is a global community that combines music, technology and charity by organizing electronic music events, the first of which took place in Dubai in 2024. The RAVE token is used for tickets and community participation.
ray: Raydium is an automated market maker (AMM) and decentralized exchange on Solana, launched in 2021. It lets users swap tokens, provide liquidity and launch new projects, and many Solana meme coins trade in Raydium pools.
re: Re (RE) is an online capital market for insurance that connects investors with fully collateralized reinsurance deals and brings them on-chain. Investors earn income from insurance premiums, which is only loosely linked to crypto market cycles.
recruit: Recruit Holdings is a Tokyo-based Japanese company in the jobs and HR technology market. It owns the job sites Indeed and Glassdoor, and in Japan runs listings platforms, staffing agencies and booking services.
red: RedStone (RED) is a blockchain oracle that feeds asset prices into DeFi smart contracts. It specializes in yield-bearing assets such as liquid staking and restaking tokens that lending markets accept as collateral; RED is used for staking and security.
rekt: Rekt (REKT) is a meme token linked to Rekt Brands, a Web3 brand spanning art, media, NFTs and physical goods. Its best-known projects are Rekt Drinks, a flavoured sparkling water marketed as the «official drink of web3», and the Rektguy NFT collection launched in 2022.
reliance: Reliance Industries is India's largest conglomerate, based in Mumbai, founded by Dhirubhai Ambani and led by Mukesh Ambani. It runs the world's largest oil refining complex in Jamnagar, the mobile operator Jio and the Reliance Retail chain.
render: Render Network is a decentralized platform where owners of graphics cards rent out computing power for 3D rendering, visual effects and AI workloads. It grew out of Jules Urbach's company OTOY; RENDER is used to pay for GPU work.
req: Request (REQ) is a network for decentralized invoices and payments, launched in 2017. Companies and freelancers issue and pay invoices in crypto with a transparent record on the blockchain; REQ tokens are burned when the network is used.
rez: Renzo (REZ) is a restaking protocol on Ethereum that works with EigenLayer: users receive the liquid token ezETH and earn extra yield for helping secure other networks. REZ is the governance token.
rice: Rice is the staple food of more than half of humanity. The Chicago exchange trades rough (unhusked) rice; prices depend on Asian harvests and export restrictions.
rif: RIF (Rootstock Infrastructure Framework) is the infrastructure token of Rootstock, a smart-contract network that runs alongside Bitcoin and is secured by its miners. RIF encourages DeFi app development on Rootstock and is used across ecosystem services.
rio-au: Rio Tinto is a British-Australian mining company founded in 1873 to work mines in Spain; these shares trade on the Sydney exchange. It mines iron ore in Australia as well as copper, aluminium and lithium.
ritual: Ritual (RITUAL) is a project building a blockchain on which smart contracts can call AI models directly. Its Infernet network connects on-chain applications with AI computation running off-chain.
river: River (RIVER) is a chain-abstraction stablecoin system: users lock collateral on one blockchain and receive the satUSD stablecoin and yield on others, without bridges. RIVER is the ecosystem's token.
rlc: iExec RLC is a French decentralized computing project from Lyon, founded in 2016. It lets developers build apps that process private data inside protected environments, and the RLC token pays for computing power and data.
rlusd: Ripple USD (RLUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched by Ripple in December 2024. It is issued under a New York trust charter, backed by dollar deposits, short-term US Treasuries and cash equivalents, and runs on both the XRP Ledger and Ethereum, mainly for payments and institutional use.
rms: Hermès is a Paris-based French luxury house founded in 1837 as a harness workshop. Today it makes the iconic Birkin and Kelly bags, silk scarves, clothing, perfumes and watches; the founder's family still holds control.
ron: Ronin (RON) is a gaming blockchain created by Vietnamese studio Sky Mavis for the game Axie Infinity. It offers cheap, fast transactions for in-game economies and NFTs, and RON is used to pay fees and for staking.
rose: Oasis Network (ROSE) is a layer-1 blockchain for confidential applications, founded by Berkeley professor Dawn Song. Its key network, Sapphire, is an EVM-compatible environment where smart contracts can work with private data; ROSE pays for fees and staking.
rpl: Rocket Pool (RPL) is a decentralized liquid staking protocol for Ethereum, founded in Australia. Users can stake from 0.01 ETH and receive the rETH token, while node operators lock up RPL as extra collateral that guarantees honest behaviour.
rsr: Reserve Rights (RSR) is the token of the Reserve protocol, where anyone can issue a stablecoin or index token backed by a basket of assets. RSR insures these tokens: it is staked as extra collateral in case the reserve loses value, and it is also used for governance.
rtx: RTX (formerly Raytheon Technologies) is a US aerospace and defense company based in Arlington, Virginia. It combines jet engine maker Pratt & Whitney, avionics supplier Collins Aerospace and Raytheon, which builds missiles and Patriot air-defense systems.
rune: THORChain is a decentralized cross-chain exchange that lets users swap native coins between blockchains, such as real Bitcoin for ETH, without bridges or wrapped tokens. RUNE is the base asset of its liquidity pools and is bonded by node operators to secure the network.
ry: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) is Canada's largest bank, headquartered in Toronto and founded in 1864 in Halifax. It serves individuals and businesses and runs wealth management, insurance and investment banking in Canada, the US and other countries.
s: Sonic (S) is an Ethereum-compatible (EVM) layer-1 blockchain that grew out of the Fantom network, whose FTM tokens were swapped for S. It focuses on fast, cheap transactions for DeFi and gives part of the fees back to app developers.
saf: Safran is a French aerospace and defence company based in Paris. Through CFM, its joint venture with GE, it makes the popular LEAP jet engines for the Airbus A320neo and Boeing 737 MAX, as well as landing gear, brakes, cabin interiors and navigation systems.
safe: Safe (SAFE), formerly Gnosis Safe, is the standard for multisignature wallets on Ethereum and other chains, where a transfer needs approval from several keys. DAOs, funds and companies use it to hold assets; SAFE is the ecosystem's governance token.
sahara: Sahara AI is a blockchain platform for decentralized AI development where anyone can build, contribute data or models and earn from it. It combines its own blockchain, a marketplace for datasets and AI agents; the SAHARA token is used for payments and governance.
samsung-electronics: Samsung Electronics is a South Korean technology giant based in Suwon, founded in 1969. It is the world's largest maker of memory chips and a leader in Galaxy smartphones, TVs and home appliances, and it also makes chips for other companies.
san-es: Banco Santander is Spain's largest bank and one of Europe's biggest, founded in 1857 in the city of Santander. It operates in Spain, the United Kingdom, Brazil, Mexico, the United States and other countries, serves well over a hundred million customers and runs a large car-finance business, Santander Consumer.
sanc: Sanctum is liquid staking infrastructure on Solana. It lets any validator or project issue its own staked-SOL token and swap such tokens with one another instantly through a shared liquidity pool called Infinity.
sand: The Sandbox (SAND) is a virtual game world on Ethereum where players buy plots of LAND as NFTs and build games and spaces from voxel objects on them. The platform is developed with backing from Animoca Brands; SAND is used for purchases, staking and voting.
sap: SAP is a German software company based in Walldorf, founded in 1972 by former IBM engineers. Europe's largest software maker, its ERP systems such as S/4HANA run finance, purchasing and production at large companies worldwide.
sap-de: SAP is Europe's largest software company, based in Walldorf, Germany, and founded in 1972 by former IBM engineers. It builds ERP systems for managing finance, purchasing, production and staff, used by most of the world's large companies.
saudi-aramco: Saudi Aramco is Saudi Arabia's state oil company, based in Dhahran, and the world's largest oil exporter. It produces oil and gas (including at the giant Ghawar field) and owns refineries and chemical plants; part of its shares were listed in 2019.
sc: Siacoin (SC) is the token of Sia, a decentralized cloud storage network launched in 2015. Users rent disk space from independent hosts around the world, files are encrypted and spread across many nodes, and storage is paid for in SC.
schd: Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity (SCHD) holds US companies with stable and growing dividends. It is popular with people building passive income.
schg: Schwab U.S. Large-Cap Growth (SCHG) holds large US growth companies at a very low fee, with a heavy tilt towards technology.
schw: Charles Schwab is one of the largest US brokers and wealth managers, founded by Charles Schwab in 1971 and now headquartered in Texas. It offers commission-free stock trading, banking and retirement accounts, and it bought TD Ameritrade in 2020.
sei: Sei is an Ethereum-compatible (EVM) layer-1 blockchain that uses parallel transaction execution for high speed. The network focuses mainly on trading, DeFi and games; SEI pays for fees and staking.
sent: Sentient is an open-source AI project building a community network of open models, agents and data as an alternative to closed AI labs. Through the Sentient GRID, partners combine models and computing power, and contributors are rewarded; SENT is the token at the core of the network's economy.
sfp: SafePal (SFP) is a crypto wallet with hardware, mobile and browser-extension versions, backed by Binance Labs. It lets users store, swap and buy cryptocurrencies across many blockchains; the SFP token gives discounts and access to wallet features.
share: ShareX (SHARE) is Web3 infrastructure for the sharing economy that puts devices such as charging stations and vending machines, along with their usage and revenue data, on the blockchain. This lets income from real-world devices be turned into tokenized assets.
shib: Shiba Inu is a meme coin featuring the Shiba Inu dog, launched in 2020 by an anonymous founder known as Ryoshi as a "Dogecoin killer". The token runs on Ethereum, and its ecosystem includes the ShibaSwap exchange and its own layer-2 network, Shibarium.
shop: Shopify is a Canadian technology company from Ottawa, founded in 2006 by Tobi Lütke. Its platform lets anyone open an online store, accept payments, manage inventory and sell through social media and in physical shops.
shop-etf: Shopify is a Canadian technology company from Ottawa, founded in 2006 by Tobi Lütke. Its platform lets anyone open an online store, accept payments, manage inventory and sell through social media and in physical shops.
shx: Stronghold (SHX) is the token of Stronghold, a US financial platform offering APIs for dollar payments, trading and settlement. SHX runs on the Stellar network and is used across the platform's ecosystem, including for rewards and discounts.
sie: Siemens is a German technology group based in Munich, founded in 1847 by Werner von Siemens. It makes factory automation equipment and industrial software, systems for buildings and power grids, and trains and rail signalling.
sign: Sign is a project building infrastructure for verifying data and distributing tokens: Sign Protocol for on-chain attestations and TokenTable for airdrops and vesting. The SIGN token is used in the ecosystem and for governance.
silver: Silver is both a precious and an industrial metal, used in electronics, solar panels and medicine. Because of that dual demand, its price usually moves more sharply than gold's.
sk-hynix: SK hynix is a South Korean memory chip maker based in Icheon and part of the SK Group. It produces DRAM and NAND flash memory and is a major supplier of HBM high-bandwidth memory used in AI accelerators, including Nvidia's.
skr: Seeker (SKR) is the token of the Solana Mobile ecosystem tied to the Seeker smartphone, successor to the Saga. It supports a decentralized app store without middlemen and community governance, letting developers reach users directly.
sky: SKY is the governance token of Sky Protocol, the new name of MakerDAO, creator of the DAI stablecoin. After the 2024 rebrand the protocol issues the USDS stablecoin (an upgraded DAI), and SKY holders vote on the system's key settings.
skyai: SkyAI is an artificial intelligence project on BNB Chain building an ecosystem of AI tools around MCP (Model Context Protocol). It connects AI agents to blockchain data and outside services, and the SKYAI token is used within that ecosystem.
slv: iShares Silver Trust (SLV) is a fund backed by physical silver — the simplest way to own silver through an ordinary brokerage account.
smh: VanEck Semiconductor (SMH) is an ETF holding the biggest chipmakers and chip-equipment companies, such as Nvidia, TSMC, Broadcom and AMD.
smic-cn: SMIC (A shares) are shares of Chinese contract chipmaker SMIC listed on Shanghai's STAR Market for tech companies. Founded in 2000, the company makes chips for Chinese and foreign designers and is the largest semiconductor foundry in mainland China.
sn51: lium (SN51) is subnet 51 of the decentralized Bittensor network, working as a cloud for renting NVIDIA GPUs for AI workloads. Users rent graphics cards via the website, command line, SDK or API, while hardware owners receive most of the rental fee.
sn64: Chutes (SN64) is subnet 64 of the decentralized Bittensor network, offering serverless compute for running AI models. Developers deploy and call models through an API, while miners supply GPUs and earn rewards.
sn75: Hippius (SN75) is subnet 75 of the decentralized AI network Bittensor, providing decentralized cloud data storage. Miners are rewarded for storing files, and SN75 is the subnet's alpha token.
snek: Snek (SNEK) is a meme token on Cardano with a snake mascot and one of the best-known meme projects in that ecosystem. It presents itself as a currency for meme creators and relies on the activity and creativity of its community.
snt: Status (SNT) is a project that combines a decentralized messenger, a crypto wallet and a Web3 browser in one app. The team is also developing Status Network on Ethereum, and SNT is used for governance.
snx: Synthetix (SNX) is a DeFi protocol founded by Australian Kain Warwick that started in 2018 as a platform for synthetic assets and now runs as a decentralized perpetual futures exchange on Ethereum. SNX holders provide collateral and govern the protocol.
sol: Solana is a layer-1 blockchain for smart contracts, DeFi, NFTs and memecoins, known for fast and cheap transactions. It launched in 2020; co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko is originally from Ukraine.
solv-token: Solv Protocol (SOLV) is a Bitcoin staking platform that issues SolvBTC, a tokenized BTC that can be used in DeFi across many networks to earn yield. SOLV is the protocol's governance token.
sony-group: Sony Group is a Japanese conglomerate based in Tokyo, founded in 1946. It makes PlayStation consoles, camera image sensors, TVs and audio gear, and owns Sony Pictures, Sony Music and a financial services business.
soon: SOON is a stack for launching layer-2 networks based on the Solana Virtual Machine (SVM) on top of different blockchains. Its Decoupled SVM design lets fast rollups with fraud proofs run on any layer 1; the project also launched a bridge between Solana and TON with a Telegram mini app.
soso: SoSoValue (SOSO) is an AI-powered crypto market research platform, best known for its summary data such as flows into bitcoin ETFs. It also runs the SSI protocol for index baskets of crypto assets; SOSO is used for rewards and governance.
soxx: iShares Semiconductor (SOXX) is a BlackRock ETF that invests in US-listed semiconductor companies: chip designers, manufacturers and equipment makers.
soybeans: Soybeans are a major source of plant protein and oil, used for animal feed, soybean oil and tofu. Brazil and the US are the largest producers and China the largest buyer.
soyoil: Soybean oil is one of the world's most widely used cooking oils and also a feedstock for biodiesel, so its price depends on energy policy as well as food demand.
space: Spacecoin (SPACE) is a satellite-based decentralized internet project building a constellation of small low-orbit satellites to give people worldwide network access without middlemen. The SPACE token is used for payments and incentives in the network.
spk: Spark (SPK) is an on-chain capital allocator in the Sky ecosystem (formerly MakerDAO) that deploys stablecoin reserves into DeFi, CeFi and real-world assets. Its products, such as sUSDS and sUSDC, give users yield; SPK is the governance and staking token.
spx: SPX6900 is a meme coin that ironically parodies the S&P 500 stock index and traditional finance culture. It has no real technological function and is a community joke about "beating" the stock index; the token exists on Ethereum and other networks.
spy: SPDR S&P 500 (SPY), launched in 1993, is the oldest US-listed ETF and tracks the S&P 500 index of 500 leading American companies — often treated as 'the market' itself.
srx: StorX (SRX) is a decentralized cloud storage service: files are encrypted, split into pieces and spread across nodes around the world. Node operators earn SRX for the space they provide, and the project runs on the XDC network.
ssv: SSV Network (SSV) is decentralized infrastructure for Ethereum staking that splits the work of one validator across several independent operators. This makes staking more reliable and secure; operators are paid in SSV tokens.
stable: Stable is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for the USDT stablecoin: network fees are paid directly in USDT rather than in a volatile token. It targets payments, cross-border transfers and businesses; STABLE is the network's token for governance and staking.
steem: Steem is a blockchain launched in 2016 that rewards users with tokens for posting and voting on useful content. The Steemit social network runs on it; in 2020, after a conflict with the community, the Hive blockchain split off from Steem.
strk: Starknet is an Ethereum layer-2 network from the Israeli company StarkWare that uses ZK-STARK cryptographic proofs to make transactions cheaper and faster. Smart contracts are written in the Cairo language; STRK is used for fees, staking and governance.
stx-token: Stacks is a network that adds smart contracts and decentralized apps to Bitcoin, relying on the security of the Bitcoin blockchain. It was founded by Muneeb Ali; STX pays network fees and powers Stacking, which earns rewards in BTC.
su: Schneider Electric is a French company from Rueil-Malmaison and a global leader in electrical equipment and industrial automation. It makes switchboards, energy-management systems, APC uninterruptible power supplies and data-centre equipment; its history goes back to 1836.
sugar: Sugar is made from sugar cane and sugar beet. Brazil is the largest exporter and turns part of its cane into ethanol, so the sugar price is linked to oil too.
sui: Sui is a layer-1 blockchain from Mysten Labs, founded by former engineers of Meta's Diem blockchain project. It uses the Move programming language and parallel transaction processing for games, DeFi and payments.
sumitomo-mitsui-fg: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) is one of Japan's three largest banking groups, based in Tokyo. Through SMBC bank it provides retail, corporate and investment banking, leasing, credit cards and brokerage in Japan and across Asia.
super: SuperVerse (SUPER), formerly SuperFarm, is a Web3 ecosystem that combines games, DeFi and AI tools. The SUPER token is used for transactions, staking, voting and access to the ecosystem's games and liquidity services across several blockchains.
sushi: Sushi (SUSHI) is the token of SushiSwap, a decentralized exchange that appeared in 2020 as a fork of Uniswap and now runs on dozens of blockchains. Users swap tokens and provide liquidity in return for a share of trading fees; SUSHI is the governance token.
swarm: SWARM ENGINE (SWARM) is an AI tool for traders that watches the market and new token launches around the clock and rates them by signals. The SWARM token is used within the project's ecosystem.
swftc: SWFTCOIN (SWFTC) is the token of SWFT Blockchain, a service for fast cross-chain crypto swaps through the SWFT Wallet app and the SwftSwap service. It also powers the project's AI services, including the SWFTGPT assistant.
sxt: Space and Time (SXT) is a blockchain database that gives smart contracts and AI verified data with a cryptographic proof that the query was correct (Proof of SQL). The project was backed by Microsoft's venture fund M12; SXT pays for queries and staking.
syn: Synapse is a cross-chain protocol that connects layer-1 and layer-2 blockchains. Through its bridges users move assets and messages between networks without middlemen, and the SYN token is used for protocol governance.
syrup: Maple Finance (SYRUP) is an onchain lending platform that lends capital to institutional borrowers against collateral and offers depositors yield through syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT. The protocol was founded in Australia in 2019; SYRUP is its governance and staking token.
t: AT&T is one of the largest US telecom operators, headquartered in Dallas. It provides mobile service, home internet and fibre networks for consumers and businesses; its history goes back to the Bell Telephone Company founded in 1877.
t-token: Threshold Network (T) was formed in 2022 by merging the NuCypher and Keep networks. It develops threshold cryptography, and its best-known product is tBTC, a decentralized bitcoin token for use on Ethereum; T is used for node staking and governance.
tag: TAGGER (TAG) is a decentralized data platform for AI where participants collect and label data for training models. The blockchain records authorship and rights to the data, and the platform lets it be sold as a commodity.
take: OVERTAKE is a smart-contract platform for trading in-game assets that replaces risky peer-to-peer deals between players. It makes ownership of game items verifiable and safe to transfer; TAKE is the ecosystem token.
tao: Bittensor is a decentralised machine-learning network where participants compete to provide AI models and computing power in specialised 'subnets'. The best performers are rewarded in TAO, whose supply is capped at 21 million, like bitcoin's.
td: TD Bank (Toronto-Dominion Bank) is one of Canada's largest banks, based in Toronto and formed in 1955 by the merger of two banks. Besides Canada, it has a large branch network on the US East Coast under the TD Bank brand.
tencent: Tencent is a Chinese tech giant based in Shenzhen, founded in 1998 by Ma Huateng (Pony Ma). It owns the super-app WeChat and the WeChat Pay payment service, is the world's largest gaming company (Honor of Kings, stakes in Riot Games and Supercell) and runs cloud services.
tfuel: Theta Fuel (TFUEL) is the operational token of the Theta network, used to pay for blockchain operations and to reward participants for relaying video streams and running computations on edge nodes. It works alongside THETA, which handles governance and security.
tgbp: Tokenised GBP (tGBP) is a stablecoin pegged 1:1 to the British pound and issued by a UK firm registered with the FCA. It is backed by cash and short-term UK Treasury bills and is used for on-chain payments in sterling.
theta: Theta Network is a blockchain for decentralized video delivery, media and AI computing. Participants share their computers' bandwidth and processing power and earn rewards; THETA is used for governance and staking, while a separate token, TFUEL, pays for operations.
tia: Celestia is a modular blockchain specializing in data availability: other networks publish their transaction data on it instead of storing everything themselves. This makes launching new blockchains and rollups easier; TIA pays for data and is used for staking.
tjx: TJX Companies is the world's largest off-price retailer of clothing and home goods, headquartered in Framingham, Massachusetts. It runs the T.J. Maxx, Marshalls and HomeGoods chains in the US and TK Maxx in Europe and Australia.
tlt: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond (TLT) holds long-term US government bonds maturing in more than 20 years. Its price reacts strongly to changes in interest rates.
tmo: Thermo Fisher Scientific is the world's largest supplier of equipment and services for science, headquartered in Waltham, Massachusetts. It sells lab instruments, reagents and consumables and manufactures medicines under contract for drug companies.
tmus: T-Mobile US is an American mobile carrier based in Bellevue, Washington, controlled by Deutsche Telekom. After merging with Sprint in 2020 it became one of the largest US wireless operators and a leader in 5G coverage.
toshi: Toshi (TOSHI) is a meme token on the Base network, named after the cat of Coinbase co-founder Brian Armstrong. The coin has become one of the symbols of Base's meme culture; it has no separate product and is driven by its community.
toyota: Toyota Motor is a Japanese carmaker based in Toyota City and one of the largest in the world, founded in 1937. It builds Toyota and Lexus cars and Hino trucks and is known for its «just-in-time» production system and the Prius hybrid.
trac: OriginTrail (TRAC) is a project from Slovenia building a decentralized knowledge graph for artificial intelligence and supply chains. It helps verify where data and goods come from, and TRAC is used to pay for publishing and storing data on the network.
trb: Tellor (TRB) is a decentralized oracle that delivers outside data, such as prices, to smart contracts on Ethereum and other networks. Data is submitted by participants who stake TRB, and they can lose their stake for reporting false information.
troll: TROLL is a Solana meme coin inspired by internet trolling culture and the famous Trollface meme. It was created for fun and community and has no utility or intrinsic value of its own.
trump: Official Trump (TRUMP) is a meme coin on Solana, launched in January 2025 on the eve of Donald Trump's inauguration and tied to his brand. The token gives no rights to any company or income — it is purely a meme and collectible asset.
truth: Swarm Network (TRUTH) is a decentralized protocol in which swarms of AI agents, together with people, check facts and data and record the results of the checks on the blockchain. The TRUTH token is used for payments, staking and rewards for network participants.
trx: TRON is a blockchain founded by Justin Sun in 2017. It is popular for sending stablecoins, above all USDT, thanks to low fees; TRX pays for network resources and is used for staking.
tsla: Tesla is an American electric car maker based in Austin, Texas, led by Elon Musk. It builds the Model 3, Model Y, Cybertruck and other cars, Powerwall and Megapack batteries for homes and the grid, and develops self-driving, robotaxis and the Optimus humanoid robot.
tsm: TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing) is the world's largest contract chipmaker, based in Hsinchu, Taiwan, and founded in 1987 by Morris Chang. It makes processors to order for Apple, Nvidia, AMD and other companies on the most advanced production processes.
tsmc: TSMC (Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company) is a Taiwanese contract chipmaker from Hsinchu, founded in 1987 by Morris Chang. As the world's largest chip foundry, it produces the most advanced processors for Apple, Nvidia, AMD and Qualcomm.
tte: TotalEnergies is a French energy company based in Paris and one of the world's largest oil and gas groups, with roots going back to 1924. It produces oil and gas, is a major LNG supplier, refines oil, runs a network of filling stations and is rapidly expanding solar and wind power.
turbo: Turbo (TURBO) is a meme coin on Ethereum created in 2023 by artist Rhett Mankind following prompts from the GPT-4 chatbot and a budget of 69 dollars. It is promoted as the first meme coin designed by artificial intelligence; the token has no practical function.
tusd: TrueUSD (TUSD) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched in 2018 by TrustToken and later sold to Techteryx, a company linked to the Tron ecosystem. Its reserves are meant to be held in dollars and short-term assets, with attestations published online, and it runs on Ethereum, Tron and other networks.
twt: Trust Wallet Token (TWT) is the token of Trust Wallet, a popular mobile crypto wallet owned by Binance since 2018. TWT holders get fee discounts inside the wallet, bonuses and a vote on how the product develops.
txn: Texas Instruments is a US semiconductor maker based in Dallas, founded in 1930. It leads in analog and embedded chips for industry and cars, is also known for school calculators, and its engineer Jack Kilby invented the integrated circuit.
ub: Unibase is a decentralized memory layer for AI agents, giving them long-term memory and the ability to work across different platforms. The project builds blockchain infrastructure for an "open agent internet"; UB is the ecosystem token.
uber: Uber is an American tech company from San Francisco, founded in 2009. Through its app people order rides with drivers, food and grocery delivery (Uber Eats) and freight transport (Uber Freight) in dozens of countries.
ubsg: UBS is Switzerland's largest bank, headquartered in Zurich and Basel. It is the world leader in managing wealth for affluent clients, and in 2023 it took over its long-time rival Credit Suisse.
ultima: Ultima (ULTIMA) is the token of the Ultima ecosystem, which runs on its own DPoS blockchain and focuses on fast, cheap everyday payments. The ecosystem includes a wallet, a payment card and other services for storing and spending the coins.
uma: UMA (Universal Market Access) is a DeFi protocol for creating financial contracts and a decentralized oracle. Its "optimistic oracle" confirms real-world events and data for smart contracts, including resolving Polymarket prediction markets; the UMA token is used for voting and settling disputes.
umxm: Manadia (UMXM) is a Web3 infrastructure project that combines AI collaboration with privacy-preserving computation. It aims to provide verifiable data settlement and private value transfer between on-chain and off-chain systems, for uses such as finance and asset digitization.
unh: UnitedHealth Group is the largest health insurance company in the United States, based in Minnetonka, Minnesota. It has two parts: UnitedHealthcare sells health insurance, while Optum runs clinics, pharmacy benefits, health data and software for hospitals.
uni: UNI is the governance token of Uniswap, the largest decentralised exchange (DEX) on Ethereum, launched in 2018 by Hayden Adams. Uniswap lets people swap tokens straight from their wallet via liquidity pools, and UNI holders vote on protocol changes.
unp: Union Pacific is the largest US railroad by track length, headquartered in Omaha, Nebraska, and founded in 1862. It hauls coal, grain, chemicals, cars and containers across a network of tens of thousands of kilometres of track in the western United States.
unp-token: Unipoly (UNP) is a GameFi project launched in October 2023 that is building a decentralized entertainment platform mixing games with real-estate-themed elements. The UNP token serves as the currency of its ecosystem.
up: Unitas (UP) is a yield-bearing stablecoin protocol from Unipay: its dollar token earns income through delta-neutral arbitrage strategies, including ones built on JLP on Solana. The UP token is tied to the protocol's governance and incentives.
uqc: Uquid Coin (UQC) is an Ethereum token linked to the Uquid online store, where shoppers can buy goods, gift cards and mobile top-ups with cryptocurrency. UQC gives discounts and is used within that ecosystem.
ura: Global X Uranium (URA) invests in uranium miners and companies in the nuclear power supply chain.
usd0: Usual USD (USD0) is a dollar stablecoin from Usual, a Paris-founded DeFi protocol launched in 2024. It is backed one-to-one by tokenized short-term US Treasury bills, and the protocol's USUAL token gives holders a share of its revenue and governance.
usd1: USD1 is a dollar-pegged stablecoin launched in 2025 by World Liberty Financial, a crypto project linked to the Trump family. Its reserves are held in short-term US Treasuries, dollar deposits and cash equivalents, with custody by BitGo, and it runs on Ethereum and BNB Chain.
usdc: USDC is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Circle, a US fintech company, launched in 2018 together with Coinbase. Each token is backed by cash and short-term US Treasuries held at regulated institutions, and it is used for payments, trading and DeFi on Ethereum, Solana and other networks.
usdd: USDD is a dollar-pegged stablecoin of the Tron ecosystem, launched in 2022 and associated with Tron founder Justin Sun. It is over-collateralized with crypto reserves such as TRX and other stablecoins, runs mainly on the TRON network and is used in its DeFi apps.
usde: Ethena USDe (USDE) is a synthetic dollar from Ethena Labs, launched in 2024. Instead of bank deposits it holds crypto such as ETH and BTC and offsets their price moves with short futures positions; staked USDe (sUSDe) earns the funding and staking income.
usdf: Falcon USD (USDF) is a synthetic dollar from Falcon Finance, a project backed by DWF Labs. Users mint it by depositing stablecoins, bitcoin, ether and other assets worth more than the USDF they receive; staking it as sUSDf earns yield from market-neutral trading strategies.
usdg: Global Dollar (USDG) is a dollar-pegged stablecoin issued by Paxos from Singapore under the city's stablecoin rules, launched in 2024. It belongs to the Global Dollar Network, whose members such as Robinhood and Kraken share the reserve income, and it runs on Ethereum and Solana.
usds: USDS is the dollar-pegged stablecoin of Sky, the protocol formerly known as MakerDAO, launched in 2024 as the upgraded successor to DAI. DAI can be swapped for USDS one-to-one, and holders can deposit it to earn the Sky Savings Rate.
usdt: Tether (USDT) is the largest stablecoin, a token designed to stay equal to one US dollar. Issued by Tether since 2014 and backed mainly by cash and US Treasury bills, it runs on Tron, Ethereum and many other networks and is widely used for trading and transfers.
useless: Useless Coin (USELESS) is a Solana memecoin launched in 2025 that openly presents itself as a "useless" token with no function at all. The whole idea is irony about crypto speculation, and its price depends only on community demand.
usual: Usual is a DeFi protocol that issues the USD0 stablecoin, backed by tokenized US Treasury bonds and other real-world assets. The USUAL token gives holders governance rights and a share of the protocol's revenue.
v: Visa is a San Francisco-based US payments company that runs the world's largest card payment network. It does not issue cards or lend money itself: banks issue Visa cards, and Visa earns a fee for processing each transaction.
vea: Vanguard FTSE Developed Markets (VEA) invests in companies from developed countries outside the US, mainly Europe, Japan, Canada and Australia.
velo: Velo (VELO) is the token of Velo Labs, a protocol for cross-border money transfers and settlement focused on Southeast Asia. It runs on the Stellar and BNB Chain blockchains and uses VELO as collateral to issue digital credit between partners in its network.
velvet: Velvet Capital (VELVET) is a non-custodial terminal for social crypto trading: spot, perpetual futures and yield strategies on Solana, Base, BNB Chain, Ethereum, Hyperliquid and other networks. Users can copy other traders' trades, and VELVET is the platform token.
verem: Verified Emeralds (VEREM) is a real-world asset project in which each token is backed by GIA-certified emeralds held in audited storage. It operates under ADGM regulatory rules in Abu Dhabi and links the gemstone market with DeFi.
vet: VeChain is a business-focused, Ethereum-compatible blockchain for supply-chain tracking, proving where goods come from and sustainability reporting. It uses two tokens: VET stores value, while the VTHO gas it generates pays for transactions.
vgt: Vanguard Information Technology (VGT) is an ETF covering the US tech sector: software, chips and hardware companies of all sizes.
vig: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation (VIG) invests in US companies that have raised their dividends for at least 10 years in a row.
virtual: Virtuals Protocol is a platform launched on Base in 2024 where users create, tokenize and monetize AI agents, including virtual characters and game bots. VIRTUAL is the base token that individual agent tokens are paired and traded against.
vnq: Vanguard Real Estate (VNQ) invests in US REITs — companies that own property such as offices, warehouses and apartments and pay out most of the rental income.
voo: Vanguard S&P 500 (VOO) tracks the S&P 500 index of 500 large US companies with one of the lowest fees available. It is a popular choice for regular long-term investing.
vr: Victoria VR (VR) is an open-source platform that turns text prompts into 3D content and virtual worlds using AI. The project started as a VR metaverse, and the VR token is used across its ecosystem.
vsn: Vision (VSN) is the Web3 ecosystem token of Bitpanda, the European crypto and investing platform from Vienna. It powers the Bitpanda DeFi wallet, the Vision Chain layer-2 network and a launchpad; holders get fee discounts, staking rewards and voting rights.
vt: Vanguard Total World Stock (VT) is a single fund for the whole world's stock market: thousands of companies from the US, Europe, Asia and emerging markets.
vtho: VeThor (VTHO) is the gas token of the VeChainThor blockchain, used to pay transaction fees. Holders of the main coin VET receive VTHO automatically, which keeps fees separate from VET's price; the network is used for supply-chain tracking and proving where goods come from.
vti: Vanguard Total Stock Market (VTI) holds the entire US stock market in one fund — thousands of companies from giants to small caps — at a very low fee.
vug: Vanguard Growth (VUG) invests in large US growth companies — firms expected to grow faster than average, mostly in technology.
vvs: VVS Finance (VVS) is a decentralized exchange with an automated market maker on Cronos, the network linked to Crypto.com. Users swap tokens, provide liquidity and stake VVS to earn rewards.
vvv: VVV is the token of Venice, a private generative AI service founded by crypto entrepreneur Erik Voorhees. Venice gives access to open-source language models, image and code generation without storing user prompts; staking VVV unlocks API access for developers and AI agents.
vwo: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets (VWO) invests in companies from emerging markets such as China, India, Taiwan and Brazil.
vxus: Vanguard Total International Stock (VXUS) invests in companies outside the United States — Europe, Japan, China and other emerging markets — in one low-cost fund.
vym: Vanguard High Dividend Yield (VYM) invests in US companies whose dividend yield is above the market average.
vz: Verizon is one of the largest US telecom operators, headquartered in New York. It provides mobile service, Fios home internet and business services; the company was formed in 2000 from parts of the former Bell system.
w: Wormhole (W) is a cross-chain protocol for passing messages and tokens between dozens of blockchains, including Ethereum and Solana. The network is verified by a group of independent «Guardian» nodes; W is used for protocol governance.
wal: Walrus (WAL) is a decentralized storage network for large files, created by Mysten Labs, the team behind the Sui blockchain. It stores video, images and AI data reliably and cheaply; WAL pays for storage and is staked by node operators.
wbt: WhiteBIT Coin (WBT) is the native token of WhiteBIT, a crypto exchange founded in Ukraine in 2018. WBT gives trading-fee discounts, access to staking and other exchange services, and is used on its own WB Network blockchain.
well: Welltower is a US real estate investment trust (REIT) based in Ohio. It owns senior housing, medical office buildings and care facilities in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom and earns money from rent and property management.
wemix: WEMIX is the blockchain and token of South Korean game publisher Wemade, known for the Legend of Mir series. The platform brings together blockchain games, NFTs and DeFi services; WEMIX serves as in-game currency and pays network fees.
wfc: Wells Fargo is one of the largest US banks, headquartered in San Francisco and founded in 1852. It serves millions of people and businesses with accounts, cards, mortgages, business loans and wealth management; its symbol is a stagecoach.
wheat: Wheat is one of the world's staple grains and the raw material for bread and flour. Its price is driven by harvests in the US, Russia, the EU and Ukraine, and by the weather.
wif: dogwifhat (WIF) is a memecoin on Solana whose mascot is a Shiba Inu dog wearing a pink knitted hat. Launched at the end of 2023, it became one of the best-known Solana memecoins; the token has no practical use, and its value rests on the community.
win: WINkLink (WIN) is an oracle in the TRON ecosystem that feeds real-world data, such as asset prices and random numbers, into smart contracts. The project grew out of the WINk gaming platform; WIN is used to pay for data and for staking.
wkc: Wiki Cat (WKC) is a BNB Chain meme token with a cat mascot, conceived as an educational project to introduce people to cryptocurrencies. It relies on community activity and has no product of its own.
wld: Worldcoin (World) is a project by Tools for Humanity, co-founded by OpenAI chief Sam Altman. Its Orb device scans the iris to confirm that a user is a unique human rather than a bot; WLD is the ecosystem's token.
wlfi: World Liberty Financial is a decentralized finance crypto project linked to Donald Trump's family. It issues the USD1 stablecoin, and the WLFI token gives holders the right to vote on how the platform develops.
wmt: Walmart is the world's largest retailer by revenue, founded in 1962 by Sam Walton in Arkansas. It runs Walmart supercenters, Sam's Club warehouse stores and an online store, and also operates in Mexico, Canada, India (Flipkart) and other countries.
wti: WTI is the US benchmark grade of crude oil, priced in New York. Its price moves with OPEC+ decisions, US output, inventories and global demand.
xai: SideShift (XAI) is a service for swapping cryptocurrencies quickly without signing up or leaving funds on the platform, supporting dozens of coins across many networks. Holders who stake the XAI token receive a share of the platform's profit.
xan: Anoma is a decentralized "operating system" for Web3 that lets developers write one app that works on any blockchain. Builders focus on product logic instead of the infrastructure of individual networks; XAN is the project's token.
xaut: Tether Gold (XAUT) is a token from Tether in which each coin represents ownership of one troy ounce of physical gold stored in a vault in Switzerland. It lets people hold and move gold on Ethereum and other networks, and holders can redeem it for the metal.
xcn: Onyxcoin (XCN) is the token of Onyx Protocol, a project that grew out of the Chain blockchain platform and develops its own Onyx network for financial applications. XCN is used for protocol governance, staking and paying network fees.
xdc: XDC Network is a hybrid blockchain from XinFin focused on international trade and trade finance, such as tokenizing invoices, letters of credit and other documents. It runs on delegated Proof of Stake; XDC pays fees and is staked by node operators.
xec: eCash (XEC) is a cryptocurrency for everyday payments that emerged in November 2020 as a split from Bitcoin Cash. It is developed by the Bitcoin ABC team led by Amaury Séchet; the network combines mining with Avalanche-based fast finality.
xle: Energy Select Sector SPDR (XLE) is an ETF on the oil and gas companies of the S&P 500, such as ExxonMobil and Chevron.
xlf: Financial Select Sector SPDR (XLF) is an ETF on the financial sector of the S&P 500: banks, insurers and payment companies.
xlk: Technology Select Sector SPDR (XLK) is an ETF holding the technology companies that belong to the S&P 500 index.
xlm: Stellar is an open network for fast, cheap money transfers and for issuing digital assets such as stablecoins. It was founded in 2014 by Jed McCaleb and Joyce Kim and is developed by the non-profit Stellar Development Foundation.
xlv: Health Care Select Sector SPDR (XLV) is an ETF on the healthcare companies of the S&P 500: drugmakers, medical devices and health insurers.
xmr: Monero is a cryptocurrency launched in 2014 with privacy switched on by default. Ring signatures and stealth addresses hide the sender, receiver and amount, making it one of the most anonymous coins.
xno: Nano (XNO) is a cryptocurrency for fast, fee-free payments, launched in 2015 under the name RaiBlocks. It uses a block-lattice structure in which every account has its own chain of blocks, so transfers confirm within seconds.
xom: ExxonMobil is one of the world's largest oil and gas companies, headquartered in Texas and formed in 1999 by the merger of Exxon and Mobil. It produces oil and gas and refines them into fuels, lubricants (the Mobil 1 brand) and chemicals.
xp: Xphere is a blockchain with a dual architecture: a main PBFT chain for fast transaction processing and a supporting proof-of-work chain for security. This way the project tries to combine scalability, security and decentralization; XP is the network's native coin.
xpin: XPIN Network is a decentralized wireless network platform that uses blockchain to link users' connection points into a global network. Participants earn XPIN tokens for providing coverage and connectivity to others.
xpl: Plasma is a layer-1 blockchain built specifically for stablecoins, above all USDT, with fee-free transfers for users. The network is Ethereum-compatible and aimed at payments and financial services; XPL is used for staking and network security.
xpr: XPR Network (XPR), formerly Proton, is a layer-1 blockchain for payments and smart contracts launched in San Francisco on EOSIO technology. It offers fee-free transfers and readable account names instead of long addresses; the WebAuth wallet and the Metal X exchange run on it.
xrp: XRP is the native coin of the XRP Ledger, launched in 2012 for fast and cheap international payments. The company Ripple uses XRP in products for banks and payment providers.
xt: XT is the token of the crypto exchange XT.com, founded in 2018. It is used for trading-fee discounts and on XT Smart Chain, an energy-efficient public blockchain with smart-contract support.
xtz: Tezos is a blockchain for smart contracts and tokens, founded by Arthur and Kathleen Breitman, with its mainnet live since 2018. Its key feature is self-amendment: XTZ holders vote on protocol changes, and the network upgrades itself without hard forks.
xvg: Verge (XVG) is a privacy-focused cryptocurrency launched in 2014 under the name DogecoinDark. It can hide users' IP addresses through Tor and I2P and uses several mining algorithms.
xvs: Venus (XVS) is the largest lending protocol on BNB Chain, launched in 2020. Users deposit crypto to earn interest or borrow against collateral, and can also mint the VAI stablecoin; XVS is the protocol's governance token.
xyo: XYO Network (XYO) is a project founded in San Diego in 2018 that collects and verifies real-world data, such as geolocation, and passes it to blockchains, AI and business systems. Nodes in the network are rewarded in XYO tokens.
yfi: yearn.finance (YFI) is a DeFi protocol on Ethereum created in 2020 by Andre Cronje that automatically moves users' funds between lending protocols for better yield. The YFI token launched with no sale to the team or investors and is used for governance.
zama: Zama is a Paris-based cryptography company that develops open-source solutions based on fully homomorphic encryption (FHE), a technology that lets data be processed without decrypting it. Its protocol brings confidential smart contracts to public blockchains; ZAMA is the protocol's token.
zano: Zano (ZANO) is a privacy-focused layer-1 cryptocurrency launched in 2019. Transactions hide the sender, receiver and amount by default; the network also lets users issue their own confidential tokens and trade on a built-in exchange.
zbcn: Zebec Network is a blockchain payments platform best known for real-time payroll, where salary streams to employees second by second. It also offers on-chain payout infrastructure and crypto cards; the project started on Solana, and ZBCN is its ecosystem token for governance and staking.
zec: Zcash is a privacy cryptocurrency launched in 2016. It uses zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs) that can fully encrypt the sender, receiver and amount; users choose between transparent and shielded transfers.
zen: Horizen (ZEN) is a privacy-focused project that began in 2017 as a fork of Zcash. It builds a modular platform that makes privacy technology such as zero-knowledge proofs easy for applications to use; ZEN is its native token.
zerebro: Zerebro is an autonomous AI agent that creates, distributes and analyses content on social media and decentralized platforms by itself. It works without human control, writing posts, music and art; ZEREBRO is the project's token on Solana.
zeta: ZetaChain (ZETA) is a layer-1 blockchain launched in 2024 to connect Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana and other networks. The team also develops ZetaLabs, a private AI app, and ZETA gives access to the service, payment discounts and voting rights.
zig: ZIG Finance (ZIG) is an on-chain finance ecosystem that aims to make institutional-grade investment products available to everyone. ZIG Chain provides the infrastructure, ZIG Markets handles distribution, and ZIG is the ecosystem's native asset.
zk: ZKsync (ZK) is an Ethereum layer-2 network built by Matter Labs that uses zero-knowledge proofs to make transactions faster and cheaper. Other projects use its ZK Stack technology to build their own chains; ZK is the governance token.
zora: Zora is an on-chain social network and creator platform on the Base network where every post can become its own token ("creator coins"). The project started as an NFT marketplace and protocol for artists; ZORA is the ecosystem token.
zro: LayerZero is an interoperability protocol that lets smart contracts on different blockchains exchange messages and tokens without classic bridges. Hundreds of apps and stablecoins use it; ZRO is the governance token. Its co-founder is Bryan Pellegrino.
zrx: 0x Protocol (ZRX) is an open protocol for swapping tokens on Ethereum and other chains, launched in 2017. Its API and liquidity aggregator are built into many wallets and apps, including Matcha; ZRX is the protocol's governance token.
